title: Senior Analyst, Inventory Planning
jd_text: Overview Who we are Collaborative. Respectful. A place to dream and do. These are just a few words that describe what life is like at Toyota. As one of the world’s most admired brands, Toyota is growing and leading the future of mobility through innovative, high-quality solutions designed to enhance lives and delight those we serve. We’re looking for talented team members who want to Dream. Do. Grow. with us. Toyota does not offer support or sponsorship of job applicants for employment-based visas or any other work authorization for this role now or in the future. You must have the right to work in the United States and not require Toyota support or sponsorship for immigration-related employment (e.g., H-1B, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, TN, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, ‘job flexibility benefits’ [also known as I-140 or Adjustment of Status portability], etc.) now or in the future. You should not apply for this role if you will require Toyota to assist with immigration support or sponsorship now or in the future. Who we’re looking for Toyota’s Inventory Planning Department is looking for a passionate and highly motivated Senior Analyst. The primary responsibility of this role is to generate demand forecasts, manage inventory plans for service parts & accessories and create facility inventory simulations. You’ll also be responsible for Identifying and supporting improvement efforts of existing best practices (Kaizen) through the effective implementation of Toyota Business Practices and TPS Principles. Reporting to the SPO, Inventory Planning Manager, the person in this role will support the Inventory Planning and Demand Forecasting short, mid and long-range goals to right size inventory, minimize costs & improve profitability while maintaining customer satisfaction performance goals for our Lexus, Toyota and Private Distributor Dealers around the world. What you’ll be doing Inventory Planning and Demand Forecasting for Service Parts identified for customer consumption throughout North America, including but not limited to: Perform system validations for inbound/outbound forecasting processes. Use rigorous logic and methods to solve difficult problems (validation errors) with effective solutions. Generate and analyze performance of planning inputs such as lead times, forecast error, demand variability, and safety stock levels to determine areas not performing to standard. Develop inventory simulation models efficiently and accurately, to provide clear impact analysis on cyclic actions and/or business objectives. Support Inventory Obsolescence root cause and countermeasure. Engage / participate in high visibility, cross functional, or team driven projects, providing inventory planning & demand forecasting expertise, analytical support, strategic solutions or execution recommendations. This includes system enhancements, innovative solutions, Cost Management and Customer Service Improvements. Ability to visualize and kaizen complex procedures and information leveraging JKK and TBP tools. Regular collaboration with Parts Supply Chain Operations, Advanced Planning, Production Strategy, and Service Parts & Accessory Development Groups. Manage and prioritize problem solving through OMDS working approach/principles. Lead Inventory Planning and Demand Forecasting crisis recovery for abnormal conditions. What you bring Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain or related field; OR equivalent experience. Knowledge of statistical techniques and concepts (e.g., time series, regression, properties of distributions, statistical tests and proper usage, etc.) and experience with relevant data tools. 5+ years of Planning, SPO Supply Operations and/or related experience. Experience in leading cross functional projects. Passion and curiosity to discover actionable inventory planning solutions. Strong ability to data-mine and analyze supply chain performance data (Enterprise Data Warehouse). Experience in data visualization and manipulation tools (e.g., Alteryx, KNIME, Power Bi, SQL, Excel, Tableau etc.) to extract data and develop presentable solutions. Assess the effectiveness and accuracy of new data sources and data gathering techniques. Strong problem solving and visualization skills. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications. Added bonus if you have Completed JKK and TBP through panel. Methodical & detail-oriented self-starter. Excellent writing and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively with all levels of management. Strong understanding of Toyota Enterprise & Data Systems (TPNA, APS, NDW, VDW, TALON, WMS). Knowledge of a variety of machine learning techniques (e.g., clustering, decision tree learning, artificial neural networks, etc.) and their real-world advantages/drawbacks. What we’ll bring During your interview process, our team can fill you in on all the details of our industry-leading benefits and career development opportunities. A few highlights include: A work environment built on teamwork, flexibility, and respect Professional growth and development programs to help advance your career, as well as tuition reimbursement Team Member Vehicle Purchase Discount Toyota Team Member Lease Vehicle Program (if applicable) Comprehensive health care and wellness plans for your entire family Toyota 401(k) Savings Plan featuring a company match, as well as an annual retirement contribution from Toyota regardless of whether you contribute (if applicable) Paid holidays and paid time off Referral services related to prenatal services, adoption, childcare, schools and more Tax Advantaged Accounts (Health Savings Account, Health Care FSA, Dependent Care FSA) Relocation assistance (if applicable) Belonging at Toyota Our success begins and ends with our people. We embrace all perspectives and value unique human experiences. Respect for all is our North Star. Applicants for our positions are considered without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, religion, military or veteran status, or any other characteristics protected by law. Have a question, need assistance with your application or do you require any special accommodations? Please send an email to talent.acquisition@toyota.com .

title: Staff Technical Program Manager - Vision AI
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Most TPM roles focus on tracking timelines, coordinating milestones, and driving execution against an established plan. This role is different. You’ll own the operational backbone of a vision AI data program, ensuring ideas move seamlessly from hypothesis to data capture to validation to a governed dataset to a commercial product. You’ll sit at the center of a complex ecosystem spanning a lean founding engineering team, capture hardware and annotation vendors, frontier AI and robotics companies, academic partners, and internal Legal, Site Operations, and Finance teams. Your mandate is to create operational continuity across these interfaces, remove friction, accelerate decisions, and maintain a disciplined path from experimentation to validated, production ready outcomes. Stord Labs is an innovation center designed to evaluate emerging logistics technologies and help redefine the future of fulfillment. Within a live micro fulfillment environment, you’ll orchestrate the full lifecycle of technical experiments, ensuring promising concepts are rigorously tested, clearly validated, and efficiently transitioned into production when they demonstrate measurable business value. This role is built for a systems oriented program leader who has operated in computer vision, ML, AI, robotics, or data intensive environments and can translate fluently between research, engineering, and warehouse operations without sacrificing speed or precision. You’ll be equally comfortable working with engineers and researchers, coordinating external partners, navigating operational constraints, and communicating outcomes to executive stakeholders. The goal isn’t simply to manage the program. It’s to build the operating system that allows a new vision AI capability to move from idea to validated data product at scale. What You'll Do: Own the evaluation lifecycle: Govern the end to end pipeline of experiments, ensuring every initiative starts with a clear hypothesis, measurable success criteria, and structured evaluation framework. Drive disciplined decisions to kill, iterate, or scale based on evidence. Run hardware and vendor evaluations: Lead structured, evidence based evaluations across capture devices, depth sensors, gloves, edge compute, and data and annotation vendors. Own RFPs, scorecards, evaluation frameworks, and vendor selection. Orchestrate the cross functional ecosystem: Serve as the primary integration point between the engineering pod and Legal, Site Operations, Finance, and warehouse operations. Coordinate requirements around consent, associate participation, scheduling, floor logistics, cost modeling, and operational readiness. Manage the data pipeline program: Drive the path from pilot capture through annotation, validation, and secure buyer delivery. Own annotation throughput and QA cadence while establishing and tracking data quality, capture yield, and delivery metrics. Manage partners and buyers: Coordinate technical and operational engagement with frontier AI and robotics companies and academic partners such as Georgia Tech. Translate customer requirements into clear program priorities and ensure datasets meet the standards required for validation and delivery. Keep governance and risk on track: Ensure consent, privacy, and data rights requirements are addressed with Legal before and throughout capture activities. Identify and retire program risks while keeping executive sponsors informed of progress, tradeoffs, and decisions. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related technical discipline. 8+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Engineering Management, or complex cross functional delivery roles. Demonstrated experience running computer vision, ML, or data pipeline programs end to end, including data collection, annotation, model training pipelines, or data platform delivery. Proven experience managing both hardware and data or annotation vendors, including RFPs, structured evaluations, scorecards, and strategic partnerships. Comfortable operating in deeply technical CV, ML, and data environments and translating between research, engineering, and operations without losing precision. Strong execution discipline and experience operating in agile, sprint based, or similar environments. Demonstrated judgment in making and driving kill, iterate, or scale decisions based on data and outcomes. High ownership and comfort operating in ambiguous, 0 to 1 environments. Bonus Points: Experience in innovation labs, R&D environments, or advanced automation programs. Familiarity with egocentric or robotics datasets, annotation platforms such as Scale, MLOps, or delivering datasets to external customers. Experience with data governance, privacy, or consent programs, including BIPA, GDPR, or CCPA requirements. Familiarity with warehouse data ecosystems and architectures, including WMS, OMS, WES, and WCS. Exposure to digital twin or simulation initiatives. Domain knowledge in warehouse automation, robotics integration, or fulfillment operations. Experience working with frontier AI companies, robotics companies, academic research institutions, or other emerging technology partners.

title: Compliance Program Manager
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Role Overview The Program Manager, Compliance is a strategic driver of Stord’s operational strength and commercial growth. This role is responsible for scaling enterprise compliance programs across OSHA, EPA, GMP, and adjacent regulatory regimes -- building the infrastructure that enables Stord to operate with confidence, win in the market, and deliver on the compliance commitments that today’s leading brands require from a fulfillment partner. A mature, well-run compliance program is not just a risk management function at Stord; it is a competitive differentiator that unlocks customer revenue, supports network expansion, and protects the business at scale. Reporting to the Director of Health, Safety & Security, this is an enterprise-level, network-wide role that operates at the intersection of compliance, operations, and growth. The Program Manager partners closely with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Finance to ensure compliance capabilities are a strength Stord leads with -- enabling the business to pursue regulated customer segments, scale into new markets, and demonstrate the program maturity that top-tier brands demand. The work product of this role is what the entire organization is built around: scalable written programs, audit frameworks, certification standards, reporting infrastructure, and regulatory intelligence systems that grow stronger as Stord grows. What This Role Owns This role owns the enterprise compliance program architecture -- the standards, written programs, audit frameworks, and governance mechanisms that define what ‘compliant’ looks like at every Stord facility. The work product of this role is what the rest of the organization is held accountable to. Specifically: Enterprise compliance program design, construction, and ownership across OSHA, EPA, GMP, GDP, DOT, and applicable state and local regulatory frameworks -- building programs from the ground up where gaps exist and elevating inconsistent standards to enterprise-grade. Regulatory intelligence: continuously monitoring rulemaking, agency guidance, and enforcement trends; converting regulatory change into updated enterprise programs before gaps become violations. Enterprise audit and inspection framework: designing the internal audit program architecture, defining scope and methodology, and building the tools and cadences that keep the network inspection-ready -- not conducting site audits, but building the system that governs them. Enterprise compliance documentation infrastructure: designing and owning the system of record for all written programs, SOPs, training requirements, certifications, and regulatory correspondence -- the single source of truth for compliance across the network. Customer and industry certification programs: GMP, GDP, CTPAT, TAPA, and other regulated operating standards required by Stord’s customer base. Regulatory agency relationships: serving as the primary compliance point of contact for OSHA, EPA, and other agencies at the program level. Enterprise compliance reporting, data, and dashboards: building the metrics infrastructure that gives the Head of HSS, senior leadership, and the broader business real-time visibility into compliance performance, risk posture, and program health across the network. Enterprise compliance training architecture: defining what training is required, for whom, at what frequency, and in what format -- building the content and governance framework that regional and site teams deliver against. Key Responsibilities OSHA Compliance Program Management Build and own Stord’s enterprise OSHA compliance program -- designing the written program architecture, establishing network-wide standards, and creating the governance mechanisms that ensure consistent compliance across every facility regardless of size, volume, or operational complexity. Maintain and update OSHA-required written programs: Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout, Respiratory Protection, Emergency Action Plans, Powered Industrial Truck programs, and others as applicable. Oversee OSHA recordkeeping standards across the network -- establishing recordkeeping protocols, auditing site-level logs for accuracy, and managing 300A summary posting requirements. Serve as the primary internal resource for OSHA compliance questions, inspection preparation, and citation response -- coordinating with Legal and the Head of HSS on formal agency interactions. Track OSHA rulemaking, enforcement priorities, and National Emphasis Programs relevant to warehouse and fulfillment operations; update programs proactively. Develop and maintain OSHA compliance self-assessment tools for use by Regional Managers and Site Managers. EPA and Environmental Compliance Build and own Stord’s enterprise EPA compliance program -- designing the framework that covers applicable Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, EPCRA, and Tier II reporting obligations across the network and scales as the facility footprint grows. Maintain environmental compliance calendars for all sites, ensuring permit renewals, required inspections, and mandatory reporting deadlines are met without exception. Manage Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans and storm water pollution prevention programs where applicable. Coordinate with Facilities and Operations on environmental requirements triggered by site construction, expansion, or changes in chemical inventory. Serve as the point of escalation for environmental incidents, regulatory notifications, and corrective actions related to EPA-regulated activities. Monitor EPA regulatory changes and enforcement activity relevant to Stord’s operations; assess impact and update compliance programs accordingly. GMP, GDP, and Regulated Operating Standards Build and own Stord’s enterprise GMP and GDP compliance programs -- designing the standards, SOPs, and qualification frameworks that enable Stord to onboard and serve regulated customers at scale across health, wellness, supplement, and pharmaceutical-adjacent accounts. Develop and maintain GMP/GDP-aligned SOPs, documentation standards, and control requirements applicable to regulated fulfillment operations. Lead readiness activities for GMP and GDP customer audits and third-party certifications -- managing pre-audit assessments, coordinating site preparation, and tracking corrective action plans post-audit. Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Operations to assess GMP/GDP requirements for new customer onboarding and ensure facilities are qualified before regulated product is received. Maintain working knowledge of FDA guidance, NSF, and other applicable standards that intersect with Stord’s customer base and product handling requirements. Build and maintain a GMP/GDP compliance library: training materials, audit checklists, SOP templates, and certification documentation for use across the network. Hazmat and Chemical Compliance Build and own Stord’s enterprise Hazardous Materials compliance program -- designing the program for our fulfillment locations, OSHA Hazard Communication, EPA chemical reporting, and state-specific requirements across the full facility network. Maintain the enterprise Hazmat program: classification standards, handling and storage requirements, labeling, SDS management systems, and spill response frameworks. Establish and maintain Hazmat acceptance criteria and screening processes to ensure sites are equipped to handle regulated materials received from customers. Coordinate Hazmat compliance requirements with Transportation, Operations, and Facilities during new site launches, customer onboarding, and facility modifications. Manage DOT compliance requirements for sites involved in the outbound transportation of regulated materials, including proper shipping papers, packaging, and labeling standards. Audit Program and Inspection Readiness Architect the enterprise internal compliance audit program from the ground up -- establishing audit scope, methodology, scoring frameworks, and corrective action workflows that give the organization a consistent, repeatable mechanism for identifying and closing compliance gaps. Conduct or coordinate compliance audits across the network, producing written findings, risk ratings, and actionable corrective action plans for site and regional leaders. Manage the enterprise corrective action tracking system for compliance findings, ensuring closure within defined timelines and verifying effectiveness. Prepare the network for external regulatory inspections and customer audits -- developing site-readiness checklists, conducting pre-audit walkthroughs, and providing on-site support during inspections where required. Maintain an inspection and audit calendar for all sites, tracking regulatory visit history, findings, and corrective action status in a centralized compliance management system. Produce regular compliance performance reporting for the Head of HSS and senior leadership, including audit scores, open findings, and trend analysis. Regulatory Intelligence and Policy Development Establish and operate a systematic regulatory intelligence function -- monitoring federal and state activity across OSHA, EPA, FDA, and DOT to identify proposed rules, final rules, and enforcement trends before they affect Stord’s operations. Translate regulatory changes into policy updates, program revisions, and implementation plans; communicate impacts clearly to the Head of HSS, Regional Managers, and site teams. Own Stord’s compliance policy library: drafting, reviewing, updating, and version-controlling all compliance-related policies and written programs. Serve as subject matter authority for compliance questions from Regional Managers, Site Managers, Operations, Legal, and Customer Success. Contribute compliance expertise to new site launch processes, automation deployments, and major operational changes to ensure regulatory requirements are built in from the start. Reporting, Data & Dashboards Build the enterprise compliance reporting infrastructure from the ground up -- designing the metrics framework, data architecture, and dashboard suite that give the Head of HSS and senior leadership a real-time, accurate view of compliance performance across the network. Define the enterprise compliance KPI set selecting the leading and lagging indicators that most accurately represent program health, regulatory risk, and operational compliance posture -- and ensuring those metrics are collected consistently across all sites. Design and own compliance dashboards that surface OSHA recordable rates, audit scores, corrective action aging, training completion rates, certification status, and regulatory inspection outcomes in a format that is actionable at the executive, regional, and site levels. Build data collection standards and reporting protocols across the network -- establishing how compliance data is captured, validated, and submitted from sites and regions to ensure the enterprise view is reliable and comparable. Develop regular compliance performance reporting cadences for the Head of HSS, Operations leadership, and the Safety and Security Steering Committee -- translating raw data into clear narratives, trend analysis, and risk-flagged summaries that drive decisions. Identify systemic compliance risks and program gaps through data analysis -- surfacing patterns across sites, regions, and regulatory domains that individual site or regional reports would not reveal in isolation. Partner with Operations, Finance, and Technology to integrate compliance data into broader business reporting platforms, ensuring compliance metrics are visible alongside operational and financial performance indicators. Maintain a compliance metrics library and reporting archive that provides the organization with historical performance data, audit trails, and the documentation needed to demonstrate program maturity to regulators, customers, and insurers. Training Governance and Compliance Capability Building Build the enterprise compliance training architecture: designing the training matrix, specifying required topics, applicable employee populations, delivery methods, and completion frequencies across all regulatory domains -- the standard that governs what compliance training looks like at every Stord site. Develop compliance training content and supporting materials for use by site and regional teams -- including written programs, quick reference guides, audit checklists, and SOP templates. Govern training completion compliance across the network through record audits and gap reporting; escalate systemic deficiencies to Regional Managers with a remediation timeline. Build and maintain a compliance resource library accessible to site and regional HSS teams, enabling consistent program delivery without requiring centralized instruction. Required Qualifications Experience 7+ years of experience in regulatory compliance, EHS program management, or a related discipline in a warehouse, fulfillment, manufacturing, or logistics environment. Demonstrated expertise across multiple regulatory domains -- OSHA, EPA, and GMP/GDP -- with hands-on program ownership experience in each. Experience managing compliance programs across a multi-site network, including audit program design and regulatory agency interaction. Track record of translating complex regulatory requirements into practical, scalable operational programs. Technical Knowledge Deep working knowledge of OSHA General Industry standards, recordkeeping requirements, and enforcement processes. Strong familiarity with EPA compliance obligations applicable to warehouse and fulfillment operations, including Tier II, SPCC, and RCRA. Working knowledge of GMP and GDP standards as they apply to regulated fulfillment, distribution, and third-party logistics. Experience with DOT Hazmat regulations (49 CFR) governing the handling, storage, and transportation of regulated materials. Proficiency with compliance management systems, audit platforms, document control tools, and regulatory tracking resources. Credentials (Preferred) CSP, ASP, or equivalent safety certification preferred. CHMM (Certified Hazardous Materials Manager) or equivalent preferred. REHS, REM, or equivalent environmental compliance credential a plus. GMP/GDP auditor certification or equivalent regulated industry compliance credential preferred. OSHA 500 or OSHA 30-hour General Industry required; advanced OSHA coursework preferred. Who You Are A regulatory expert, not a generalist -- you have deep knowledge in at least two of the core compliance domains and the intellectual curiosity to go deep in the others. A program architect -- you build compliance infrastructure that scales across dozens of sites without requiring your personal presence at each one. Your programs are self-sustaining by design. Proactive and ahead of the curve -- you’re tracking rulemaking before it becomes a requirement and updating programs before an inspector identifies the gap. A credible advisor -- Regional Managers and site teams bring you their hardest compliance questions because you give clear, practical answers grounded in the actual regulation. Detail-oriented without losing the thread -- you can manage a 30-site audit calendar and still see the systemic risk patterns that individual findings represent. A strong written communicator -- your policies are readable, your audit reports are actionable, and your regulatory summaries make complex requirements understandable to operators.

title: VP, Fulfillment Planning and Optimization
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Stord is looking for a VP, Fulfillment Planning & Optimization to lead the end to end process of translating customer demand into operational readiness across our fulfillment network. This leader will own Stord’s Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process, turning customer and order forecasts into a clear operating plan for the labor, infrastructure, training, and support required to meet demand. Sitting at the intersection of Customer Experience, Operations, and Operations Support, this leader will program manage the full planning cycle from demand forecasting and operational requirements through resource deployment, performance tracking, and reforecasting, ensuring the network is positioned to deliver against customer commitments efficiently and at scale. What You'll Do: S&OP & Demand Planning: Own Stord's S&OP process across the fulfillment network, creating a single operating view of expected customer demand and the resources required to support it. Partner with CX and customers to understand expected order volume, promotions, launches, seasonality, and other demand drivers. Translate customer forecasts into site, process, shift, and time specific operating requirements. Validate customer forecasts using leading operational indicators, including inbound inventory and historical demand patterns. Identify forecast risk early and develop clear scenarios for expected, upside, and downside demand. Establish a consistent planning cadence across customers, sites, and support functions. Labor Planning : Translate demand into a comprehensive workforce plan across Stord's fulfillment network. Determine labor requirements by site, shift, process path, and planning horizon. Partner with Operations and People teams to ensure hiring, staffing, scheduling, and training plans can support forecasted demand. Track labor demand against actual labor delivery and surface gaps early enough to intervene. Build planning models that account for productivity, attendance, attrition, ramp curves, seasonality, and other operational realities. Continuously improve the accuracy and responsiveness of Stord's labor planning models. Operational Readiness : Translate the operating forecast into clear requirements for the teams responsible for enabling Operations. The forecast should trigger a coordinated readiness plan across: MHE: Equipment, capacity, maintenance, and material handling requirements. EHS & Facilities: Building readiness, safety requirements, space, and facility capacity. Procurement: Supplies, packaging, equipment, and other operating inputs. Industrial Engineering & Continuous Improvement: Capacity, process design, building layout, productivity, and future state operating models. Training: Training capacity, onboarding requirements, cross training, and workforce readiness. Ensure these teams understand what is coming, what Operations will require, when it is needed, and whether delivery is on track. Readiness Program Management : Own the program management layer connecting S&OP to execution. Translate the S&OP plan into specific requirements, owners, milestones, and delivery dates across support functions. Maintain a single view of operational readiness across the network. Track dependencies and escalate risks before they become operational failures. Hold teams accountable for delivering the resources required to support forecasted demand. Create clear executive visibility into where the network is ready, where it is at risk, and where intervention is required. Actuals, Feedback & Continuous Replanning : Close the loop between planning and reality. Once volume begins flowing through the network, this leader owns the process for understanding: What did we forecast? What actually happened? Why was it different? What needs to change now? Monitor actual inbound and outbound volume against forecast. Measure forecast accuracy by customer, site, and planning horizon. Use actual inbound volume and other leading indicators to continuously validate and refine outbound forecasts. title: VP, Inventory Control & Quality Assurance
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. About the Role Stord is looking for a Vice President of Quality to build and lead the quality function across our fulfillment network. This leader will own the systems, standards, and operating mechanisms that ensure inventory is accurate, processes are followed, and every order moves through our network the way it was designed to. The mandate spans the full lifecycle of inventory inside our buildings from inbound receipt and putaway through picking, packing, sorting, and outbound shipment. This is an independent quality function. While our Operations teams are responsible for delivering volume efficiently, the VP of Quality is responsible for ensuring we never achieve speed, growth, or cost improvements by compromising inventory integrity or execution quality. This leader should be an inventory and fulfillment quality expert at heart — someone who understands how inventory moves through a complex fulfillment operation, knows where process breakdowns create downstream failures, and is relentless about identifying and eliminating root causes. What You'll Own Inventory Health & Accuracy Own inventory health and accuracy across Stord's fulfillment network. Establish the standards, controls, and operating mechanisms required to maintain book-to-floor and floor-to-book inventory integrity. Own cycle counting, inventory reconciliation, adjustment governance, and inventory variance reduction. Build mechanisms to identify inventory defects early and systematically eliminate their root causes. Establish network-level metrics and reporting that make inventory health visible and actionable. Fulfillment Process Quality Own process adherence across inbound, receiving, putaway, picking, packing, sorting, and outbound operations. Define the critical quality controls for each process path and ensure sites consistently execute against them. Build audit mechanisms that identify process drift before it becomes a customer or inventory issue. Partner with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Data to eliminate systemic sources of defects. Develop a clear view of transaction volume, exception rates, and defect rates by process path to identify where quality is breaking down. Lot Control & Regulatory Compliance Own lot, expiration-date, and inventory-attribute accuracy across applicable customers and facilities. Establish controls for FIFO, FEFO, lot traceability, recalls, quarantine, and other regulated inventory requirements. Ensure Stord's operating processes meet applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual quality requirements. Build a quality organization capable of supporting increasingly complex and regulated categories as Stord grows. Continuous Improvement Build a rigorous root-cause and corrective-action discipline across the fulfillment network. Turn recurring defects into permanent process, system, or training improvements rather than repeatedly solving individual incidents. Identify network-wide trends and deploy standardized improvements across sites. Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure recurring operational defects inform the technology roadmap. Create a culture where defects are surfaced quickly, investigated objectively, and permanently resolved. Quality Organization Build and lead Stord's network Quality and Inventory Control organization. Establish clear ownership and accountability between Quality and Operations. Develop site and regional quality leaders capable of independently auditing operational performance. Serve as the executive escalation point when inventory integrity, regulatory compliance, or fulfillment quality is at risk. Maintain an independent point of view and be willing to stop, challenge, or redesign processes when quality standards are not being met. What We're Looking For We are looking for someone who has spent their career inside large, complex fulfillment or distribution operations and understands inventory at a level most operators do not. The ideal candidate: Has 12+ years of experience across fulfillment quality, inventory control, operational excellence, distribution, or supply chain operations, including significant leadership experience. Has led quality or inventory control across a multi-site fulfillment or distribution network . Comes from a scaled 3PL, retailer, e-commerce fulfillment network, food distribution company, or similarly complex physical operation. Is deeply fluent in inventory control, WMS-driven processes, cycle counting, reconciliation, lot control, and inventory accuracy . Understands the mechanics of inbound, putaway, pick, pack, sort, and outbound processes — and how defects in one process create downstream failures elsewhere. Has built quality systems based on data, audits, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and measurable defect reduction. Is comfortable challenging Operations leadership when execution does not meet the required standard. Has operated in environments where quality and compliance cannot be traded for throughput or cost . Ideally brings experience from food, grocery, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another environment with rigorous lot, expiration, traceability, or regulatory requirements. Can operate strategically at the executive level while still being willing to go onto the warehouse floor, trace an inventory discrepancy through a WMS, and understand exactly where a process failed.

jd_text: Who We Are Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. You'll use digital analytics for troubleshooting and apply basic diagnostic techniques to assess and address technical issues. Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. Additionally, you'll coordinate and communicate directly with customers to ensure smooth operations and exceptional service. Field Service Engineer - Process Diagnostics & Control (PDC) Be the Eyes of the Fab. Power the Future of Technology. At Applied Materials, we're helping build the technology that powers AI, cloud computing, autonomous vehicles, smartphones, and the next generation of semiconductor innovation. Our equipment is used to produce virtually every advanced chip in the world, and we're looking for talented engineers to help keep those systems performing at their best. What You'll Do As a Process Diagnostics & Control (PDC) Field Service Engineer , you'll be the trusted technical expert supporting advanced inspection and metrology systems within some of the world's most sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing facilities. These systems are often referred to as the "eyes of the fab" because they monitor, measure, and help control critical manufacturing processes that determine wafer quality and production success. In this role, you'll: ✅ Troubleshoot highly complex technical issues ✅ Perform preventative and corrective maintenance ✅ Install, qualify, and upgrade advanced semiconductor equipment ✅ Analyze performance data, logs, and diagnostics ✅ Support customer escalations and drive root-cause analysis ✅ Work alongside process engineers, equipment engineers, and fab leadership ✅ Make a direct impact on semiconductor manufacturing performance and uptime No two days are the same. One day you may be resolving an optics alignment issue. The next, you may be diagnosing a vacuum system fault or partnering with engineering teams to improve tool performance. What You'll Work On You'll support cutting-edge technologies that may include: Advanced inspection systems Metrology equipment Optical systems Laser technology Electron beam systems Vacuum systems Precision motion control systems Semiconductor manufacturing platforms What Makes Someone Successful? Successful PDC Engineers are: Natural troubleshooters Curious and analytical Comfortable working directly with customers Strong communicators Calm under pressure Passionate about continuous learning If you're the person others call when complex equipment stops working, you'll likely thrive in this role. title: Retail Insights Manager (Sales Engineer)
jd_text: Description: SPS Commerce is a leading provider of cloud-based supply chain management solutions, serving a global network of retail trading partners. We foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment where innovation and continuous improvement are highly valued. Join SPS Commerce and be part of a dynamic team that's transforming the global retail supply chain! Position Summary: As a Retail Insights Manager (Sales Engineer), you’ll be the customer-facing subject matter expert on retail deductions, chargebacks, and compliance — the person suppliers trust in the room. Partnering side by side with Account Executives and Account Managers, you’ll co-pilot deals from first demo through close, translating deep retailer knowledge into clear, compelling business cases that help suppliers protect revenue and recover deductions. This is a highly external, sales-facing role: you’ll spend the majority of your time on demos, discovery, and data presentations, acting as the technical account leader who speaks to the platform, interprets audit findings, and builds the ROI story. You came up on the supplier side managing deductions and compliance — now you’ll bring that expertise to the table for suppliers who were once in your shoes. If you thrive on meeting new people, thinking on your feet, and turning complex retail data into a story that closes business, this role puts you at the heart of how SPS Revenue Recovery drives growth for suppliers. What You'll Do: Sales-cycle co-pilot: Partner with Account Executives and Account Managers as the technical expert across the full deal cycle — first call, discovery, demo, data presentation, and contract negotiation — owning the deductions and retailer expertise the salesperson can’t carry alone. Product demos & presentations: Present and demo the SPS Revenue Recovery platform to prospects ranging from Fortune 100 suppliers to small businesses, showing deep retailer knowledge and answering questions with command and credibility. Data presentation & business case: Interpret audit and deduction analysis, pull out the insights that matter, and build the ROI and value story — then deliver it clearly to stakeholders up to and including CFO-level decision-makers . Deal strategy: Prep with reps on huddles and prep calls, strategize on messaging and outreach voice, and proactively push deals forward — weighing in on what’s best for the deal at any given moment. Retailer subject matter expertise: Serve as the go-to SME on deduction codes, compliance programs, and root-cause analysis across multiple retailers — Walmart, Amazon, Target and beyond (CVS, Walgreens, Kohl’s, Home Depot, Lowe’s, UNFI, and others we support). Cross-functional partnership – Marketing , Product Customer Success : Work close ly with Marketing — translating the voice of the supplier, advising on feature priorities, escalating data questions, and representing the retailer domain internally and externally . Hosting webinars and lead in person -events related to Revenue Recovery . Product Development : Work closely with the Revenue Recovery Product Managers to advise on feature prioritization . Sitting in on customer research calls to “ translate” user feedback . Providing insights and feedback on the product b ased on experience . Advising on potential feature opportunities and technological advancements in the platform as an SME. Thought leadership & enablement: Contribute to article creation, host webinars, support events, and help build out platform functionality as an SME — elevating the team’s external voice in the revenue recovery space. Confidentiality & trust: Handle sensitive client and revenue data with discretion and integrity while influencing strategic decisions across teams. Perform other duties as assigned. What You'll Bring: Proven Experience: Bachelor’s degree plus 2+ years of relevant experience (or equivalent education and work experience), ideally on the supplier side managing deductions, chargebacks, and retailer compliance — within a B2B SaaS, CPG, retail, or supply chain environment. Multi-Retailer Knowledge (must-have): Deep, hands-on expertise across at least two of the big three — Walmart, Target, and Amazon — with Amazon strongly preferred. Amazon-only is not sufficient; this role requires breadth across multiple retailers, as you’ll be expected to be the expert on any retailer a supplier brings to the table. Revenue Recovery Expertise: Expert-level understanding of the retailer deductions space — deduction codes, compliance programs, root-cause efforts, and how it all impacts suppliers’ day-to-day operations, including EDI and how supplier operations work. External & Sales-Facing Command: Comfortable and confident presenting to new people you’ve never met — from analysts to CFOs — and speaking to ROI on high-value contracts. Able to step into and out of complex supply chain sales cycles with high impact and credibility. Clear, Confident Communicator: Clear, concise, and confident verbal, non-verbal, and written communication — including altering vocal tone and inflection, active listening, and writing relevant, engaging content. No wallflowers: you jump in when the moment strikes. Tech-Savvy: Proficient in Microsoft Excel and Office Suite (advanced Excel — pivot tables, formulas — a plus ). Multitasking Under Pressure: Able to juggle multiple demos, presentations, and requests in a single day in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment where the calendar is rarely your own — prioritizing quickly and setting boundaries with reps. Self-Driven & Collaborative: Proactive, high-ownership, and able to work autonomously with minimal supervision, while collaborating closely and communicating well over Slack and Zoom with a distributed team. Preferred Qualifications: Knowledge of additional retailers we support (CVS, Walgreens, Kohl’s, Home Depot, Lowe’s, UNFI, and others). Power BI and/or Tableau experience. CRM tools (Salesforce) experience. Familiarity with AI tools (e.g., Claude) to support analysis, decks, and process efficiency. Mid-level ERP knowledge (most integrations involve pre-built adapters). Prior CPG, retail, supply chain, or SPS Commerce / SupplyPike experience. Where You'll Work: This role is either hybrid out of one of our offices in Minneapolis, MN, Rogers, AR or open to remote. We Succeed Together through in-person collaboration, balanced with remote work to provide flexibility What We Offer: At SPS Commerce, we are committed to ensuring that each employee’s compensation reflects their unique experiences, performance, and skills in their role. The salary range for this role considers several factors, including education, relevant skills, work history, certifications, location, and more. The annual salary range for this role is: $79,900.00 – $119,900.00 USD, plus commission. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the factors listed above and may fall anywhere within the range. SPS Commerce offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees’ health, well-being, and financial security. Benefits are country-specific and aligned with local laws and market practices. #LI-TB1 Commitment to our Employees: At SPS we power connections that drive the world of commerce forward, and our success depends on making strong decisions, fostering innovation, delivering unparalleled customer solutions, and driving outstanding business performance. We achieve this by creating an environment where every employee feels a true sense of belonging. We embrace diversity, equity, and inclusion, ensuring everyone feels accepted, valued, and empowered to make a meaningful impact. We are committed to affirmative action and equal opportunity in all aspects of employment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

title: Corporate Counsel
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. About the role: Stord is seeking a Corporate Counsel to support Stord’s commercial contracting growth as the company scales its sales pipeline by over 50%. This role will primarily focus on sales, partnerships, and commercial relationships, including reviewing, advising, and negotiating customer agreements, partner agreements, vendor contracts, amendments, and NDAs. This role will leverage AI tools alongside strong legal judgment to drive efficiency. Critical skills for this role include agility, comfort operating in ambiguity, attention to detail, and the ability to be resourceful while managing multiple initiatives. This role will work within Stord Legal and directly with the business team to understand objectives and develop business-centric strategies that mitigate risk while enabling the business to move quickly. This role will assist in providing day-to-day advice to the business team on a range of matters, including contract interpretation, strategic advice, and general inquiries. Stord is looking for a self-starter with a bias for action who thrives in a high-growth environment. What You'll Do: Partner with the Sales and Partnerships teams to review, negotiate, and execute commercial contracts, including customer agreements, reseller and referral agreements, strategic partnership agreements, and vendor contracts, while collaborating cross-functionally with the Operations, Finance, and Product teams. Own and continuously refine Stord's contract playbooks and negotiation guardrails, including fallback positions, escalation thresholds, and approval authority, to drive consistency and speed across the sales pipeline. Partner with Sales Operations and other cross-functional stakeholders to help build out Stord's contract management infrastructure as it scales, including template libraries, workflow tools, and process documentation. Support and guide the sales team and various business teams on deal structure, contract negotiations, and risk assessment, balancing legal risk with business objectives. Serve as a legal point of contact for the Sales and Partnerships teams, enabling deal velocity while managing risk. Identify opportunities to improve the contract management process to drive operational efficiencies and process standardization throughout Stord. Address internal inquiries regarding contractual questions, obligations, and compliance. Stay up to date on relevant industry, commercial, intellectual property, privacy and compliance issues. Basic Qualifications: 3+ years of experience with commercial transaction experience in the ecommerce or logistics space Experience negotiating, drafting, and solving issues for various types of commercial contracts, including those relating to warehousing and logistics, with demonstrated business judgment and ability to provide practical, risk-balanced advice. Proven ability to ramp quickly and take ownership of a contract portfolio in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with legal technology, including AI-assisted contract review tools and CLM platforms (Ironclad experience a plus) J.D. from an accredited law school and membership in at least one state bar required. Preferred Qualifications Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal, with a collaborative approach Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently to prioritize work, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines. Comfort building and refining process and structure where none fully exists yet, rather than relying solely on an established system. Logistics experience; in-house experience. Experience with warehouse liens, bailment law, or UCC Article 7 (warehouse receipts and documents of title). Familiarity with FMCSA broker regulations, transportation law, or logistics compliance requirements. Experience with data privacy agreements, technology contracts, or software licensing arrangements.

About the Role The Regional Manager, Health, Safety, Compliance & Loss Prevention is responsible for executing and continuously improving Stord's HSS program across a defined region of fulfillment and warehouse facilities. Reporting to the Head of Health, Safety, and Security, this role translates enterprise standards into daily operational reality — driving consistent performance across sites, building regional team capability, and owning outcomes. Regional Manager hires, develops, and directs a team of site-level safety and loss prevention professionals, holding them accountable to program standards while coaching them to grow. Success is measured by regional safety performance, loss prevention effectiveness, compliance posture, and the strength of the team built to sustain a culture. **This is a remote role, however must be based out of Dallas, TX with the ability to travel 40-50%.** What This Role Owns Regional Managers are active partners in program design, governance, and policy-setting — contributing regional insight, operational context, and field intelligence to enterprise decisions led by the Head of HSS. They own translating those standards into consistent regional execution and are accountable for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that drive financial, operational, and asset loss across their region. The Regional Manager is accountable for: Regional safety, compliance, and loss prevention performance metrics and trend improvement. Translating enterprise standards into site-level execution — ensuring consistent, high-quality program delivery across every facility in the region. Hiring, onboarding, and developing a regional team of HSS and loss prevention professionals. Loss prevention strategy and shrink reduction for their region — including investigation oversight, security controls, and carrier/vendor accountability. Regional compliance posture across OSHA, state regulations, and Stord internal standards. Escalation management: serving as the regional decision-maker for incidents, investigations, and regulatory inquiries. Risk ownership: proactively identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks across the region that could result in financial loss, operational disruption, or damage to people and assets — before they become incidents. Key Responsibilities Team Leadership and Development Recruit, hire, and onboard site-level safety and loss prevention professionals within the region. Set clear performance expectations, conduct regular coaching conversations, and deliver structured feedback and development plans. Build a high-accountability, growth-oriented team culture within the regional HSS function. Identify talent gaps and succession needs; develop internal candidates for expanded roles. Facilitate regional team meetings, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving across sites. Safety Program Execution Deploy and sustain enterprise safety standards across all regional facilities, ensuring consistent implementation. Conduct or oversee facility safety audits, gap assessments, and corrective action tracking. Support site leaders and operations teams in embedding safety into daily standard work and leadership routines. Lead or oversee incident investigations within the region, ensuring root cause analysis quality and timely corrective action closure. Represent the region in enterprise safety forums, surfacing trends, risks, and improvement opportunities to the Head of HSS. Coordinate peak readiness reviews to ensure safety standards are maintained through volume surges and labor onboarding. Loss Prevention and Asset Protection Own regional loss prevention strategy, including shrink reduction targets, security controls, and investigative outcomes. Oversee internal investigations related to theft, fraud, and inventory discrepancy — escalating to HR, Legal, or Law Enforcement as appropriate. Analyze loss trends across the region and drive root cause resolution through operational and procedural improvements. Manage CCTV, access control, and physical security standards across regional sites, partnering with facilities teams on remediation. Build relationships with carrier partners, vendors, and law enforcement contacts to support loss prevention outcomes. Partner with Operations and Finance to quantify and report on shrink, damage, and loss impact at the regional level. Compliance and Regulatory Management Ensure all regional facilities maintain compliance with applicable OSHA, state, and local regulations. Serve as the regional point of contact for regulatory inspections, responding to inquiries and coordinating any required corrective actions. Monitor regulatory changes with regional applicability and coordinate with the Head of HSS to update procedures accordingly. Oversee Hazmat compliance within the region, including proper storage, labeling, training, and incident reporting. Support site-level readiness for customer-required certifications such as GMP, GDP, CTPAT, or TAPA where applicable within the region. Metrics, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement Own regional safety and loss prevention KPIs, delivering regular performance reporting to the Head of HSS and regional operations leadership. Drive trend analysis across regional sites to identify systemic risks before they become incidents. Manage corrective action pipelines within the region, ensuring timely closure and verified effectiveness. Champion near-miss and hazard reporting culture across sites, tracking participation rates as a leading indicator. Partner with Ops Excellence to integrate safety and loss prevention improvements into standard operating procedures. New Site Launches and Network Changes Lead HSS readiness for new site launches within the region, including safety walkthroughs, program onboarding, and staff training. Support automation and equipment commissioning activities from a safety perspective within the region. Ensure staffing and program coverage scales appropriately as the regional network grows. Required Qualifications Experience 7+ years of experience in health and safety, loss prevention, or operations compliance. 3+ years of direct people management experience, with a track record of hiring and developing high-performing teams. Multi-site experience in 3PL, eCommerce fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing environments. Demonstrated experience in loss prevention investigation, shrink management, or asset protection in a high-volume logistics or retail environment. Technical Knowledge Working knowledge of OSHA standards, state-specific safety regulations, and compliance program management. Hands-on experience managing physical security systems, including CCTV, access control, and inventory protection protocols. Familiarity with incident investigation methodologies and corrective action systems. Comfort with Hazmat regulations and controlled substance handling requirements in a warehouse or fulfillment context. Experience using safety and loss prevention data to drive operational decisions. Credentials (Preferred) ASP, CSP, or equivalent safety certification, or active pursuit of one. Wicklander-Zulawski (WZ), Reid Technique, or equivalent interviewing certification preferred. Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement background a plus. Familiarity with CTPAT, TAPA, or SOC-related security requirements a plus. Leadership Profile A builder and developer of people — energized by growing a team, not just managing one. Highly credible with frontline associates and site operations leaders; earns trust through presence and follow-through. Capable of holding the line on standards while maintaining strong, collaborative relationships with operations partners. Analytical and data-driven; able to translate metrics into clear narratives and actionable plans for regional and executive audiences. Comfortable in ambiguity — able to triage competing priorities, escalate appropriately, and keep the team focused under pressure. Strong written and verbal communicator; able to represent the region in enterprise forums and deliver clear guidance to site teams.

title: OnSite Specialist - Austin, TX
jd_text: Work Flexibility: Field-based As an Endoscopy OnSite Specialist, you will play an essential role in supporting surgical teams and ensuring that equipment, processes, and information flow smoothly to help drive exceptional patient care. What You Will Do •Prepare, manage, and maintain surgical equipment and disposable products to ensure everything is available, functional, and ready before each procedure, achieving full equipment readiness and minimizing workflow interruptions. •Support operating room teams during procedures by anticipating device needs, providing timely equipment adjustments, and ensuring a seamless surgical experience. •Troubleshoot and resolve both routine and complex equipment issues using independent judgment to maintain high service reliability and reduce downtime. •Collaborate with surgeons, operating room personnel, central processing, biomedical staff, and other clinical partners to deliver excellent service and build strong working relationships. •Maintain accurate documentation, including detailed procedure information, equipment usage, monthly performance metrics, and account updates to ensure compliance and continuity of service. •Stay current through ongoing training, maintaining a strong working knowledge of Stryker equipment, disposable products, and new technologies while educating clinical staff on product use. •Follow all safety, facility, and privacy standards, including patient confidentiality requirements, while maintaining a professional appearance, work ethic, and customer-focused mindset. •Provide flexible coverage, including rotating schedules, on-call, overnight and weekend shifts, and support for other accounts within and outside your region, which may require travel. What you will need: Preferred Qualifications •Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree, or equivalent certifications. •1+ year of experience in customer service, technical assistance, clinical support, supporting sterile workflow operations, or operating room environments. •Knowledge of anatomy, surgical procedures, and instrumentation. •HSPA/CRCST certification (required within 6 months for Sterile Processing roles; renewed annually). Required Qualifications •High School Diploma or equivalent. •0+ years of related work experience. •Ability to work rotating schedules, including on-call, overnight, and weekend shifts, and maintain readiness to arrive within 45 minutes when on call. •Ability to lift up to 50 lbs occasionally and 20 lbs frequently; ability to stand, walk, bend, stoop, and use fine motor skills for extended periods. •Visual acuity (corrected), color vision, mobility, and dexterity to identify and correct small inconsistencies in equipment or documentation. •Strong analytical, problem-solving, and time-management skills with the ability to make independent decisions in high-pressure environments. •Ability to clearly explain and follow detailed guidelines and procedures. •Proficiency with basic computer applications (e.g., Microsoft Office) and strong interpersonal, verbal, written, and organizational skills. •Ability to travel and provide coverage at other accounts as needed, including occasional overnight travel. Scope of Work Summary (Operating Room Support): The OnSite Specialist provides in-room support for minimally invasive surgical (MIS) and related procedures, ensuring optimal performance of Stryker and third-party equipment. This role bridges clinical teams, SPD, and Stryker service lines to maintain smooth, high-quality OR operations. Core Responsibilities: · Set up Stryker towers, booms, lights, and integrated suite systems per surgeon preference. · Confirm equipment functionality and image routing prior to each procedure. · Adjust camera, monitor, and device settings intraoperatively. · Provide immediate troubleshooting of endoscopy and integration systems. · Manage post-procedure breakdown and staging of all Stryker equipment. · Clean/disinfect towers and components, restock consumables, and perform basic maintenance. · Educate OR and SPD staff on proper use and troubleshooting of Stryker products. · Support video conferencing, DICOM transfers, and EMR connectivity (where applicable). Qualifications: · Experience in OR technical support or surgical services. · Familiarity with MIS procedures (laparoscopy, arthroscopy, cystoscopy, hysteroscopy, etc.). · Excellent communication and troubleshooting skills. Scope of Work Summary (Sterile Processing Department – SPD): Responsible for reprocessing and managing surgical instrumentation per IFU, HSPA/AAMI standards, and hospital policy. Works alongside SPD staff to ensure timely, compliant reprocessing of Stryker and hospital-owned instruments. Core Responsibilities: Decontaminate and assemble rigid scopes, cameras, light cords, and power instrumentation. Perform in-line function testing (leak, sharpness, insulation, or power checks). Wrap and containerize sets for sterilization per IFU. Maintain and update Stryker-managed instrumentation lists in collaboration with SPD leadership. Facilitate repairs, replacements, and instrument tracking per hospital protocols. Communicate with SPD and OR leaders regarding equipment readiness and process improvements. Certifications: CRCST required within 6 months of hire (per Stryker and state legislation). Ongoing annual continuing education required.
