title: Project Manager III, CAAT
jd_text: Job Title Project Manager III, CAAT Agency Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi Department Autonomy Research Institute Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Corpus Christi, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description TAMU-CC is a dynamic university designated as both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and Minority-Serving Institution (MSI) with approximately 11,000 students from 47 states and 54 foreign nations. We employ over 1,400 full-time and 2,000 part-time Islanders (including students/GAs). The University attracts highly talented faculty and staff and offers an array of undergraduate and graduate degrees, including doctoral programs. As a member of the Texas A&M University System, TAMU-CC benefits from a range of resources, increased visibility and influence, and opportunities to collaborate in mutually beneficial ways with peers across member institutions and associated agencies. TAMU-CC’s beautiful campus is located on a 240-acre island on Corpus Christi Bay and was ranked #1 College by the Sea by Best College Reviews. Our natural setting is enhanced by its modern, attractive, and state-of-the-art classroom buildings and support facilities. PURPOSE The Project Manager III, CAAT manages assigned projects and task orders for the Center for Advanced Aviation Technologies (CAAT) and provides project management and coordination support for other CAAT projects, programs, consortium activities, working groups, and Autonomy Research Institute (ARI) activities as directed. This position is responsible for planning, coordinating, tracking, documenting, and reporting assigned project activities across CAAT staff, ARI support offices, CAAT Consortium members, external partners, subcontractors, and public-agency stakeholders. The position supports the Project Director, CAAT, by managing assigned project scope, schedules, deliverables, action items, risks, project records, proposal inputs, statement of work support, working group facilitation, and inputs for sponsor-facing reporting. This position is based in Fort Worth, Texas. The Project Manager III for the Center for Advanced Aviation Technologies (CAAT), operating under the general direction of the Project Director, CAAT, is responsible for managing assigned CAAT projects and task orders from initiation through execution and closeout. This role may serve as the lead Project Manager for assigned projects or provide project management and coordination support to other CAAT Project Managers on additional CAAT projects, programs, consortium activities, working groups, and ARI coordination activities as directed. This role coordinates and maintains project schedules, action item logs, project records, risk and issue trackers, deliverable trackers, meeting documentation, proposal inputs, statement of work support, working group coordination materials, and project reporting materials. This position also coordinates with ARI offices and personnel when CAAT projects require support related to finance, contracting, task order administration, research administration, operational support, or other ARI-support functions. RESPONSIBILITIES Project Management and Execution: 40% Manage assigned CAAT projects and task orders from initiation through execution and closeout. Provide project management and coordination support for other CAAT projects, programs, and activities under the direction of CAAT Project Managers or the Project Director, CAAT, as well as ARI activities that align with CAAT operational requirements. Develop and maintain project plans, schedules, task lists, milestones, deliverable trackers, risk and issue logs, action item logs, and project coordination tools for assigned projects. Coordinate project activities with CAAT personnel, CAAT Consortium members, ARI support offices, subcontractors, external partners, subject matter experts, and public-agency stakeholders to support project schedules, deliverables, dependencies, and coordination requirements. Lead and coordinate project meetings for assigned projects, including kickoff meetings, recurring project meetings, technical interchange meetings, partner coordination meetings, and closeout meetings. Track project deadlines, deliverable requirements, decisions, responsible parties, dependencies, and follow-up actions. Monitor assigned projects for schedule conflicts, scope concerns, missing inputs, overdue actions, documentation gaps, and emerging risks; escalate issues to the Project Director, CAAT, or CAAT Project Managers as appropriate. Coordinate project startup activities, including project file setup, schedule development, contact list development, kickoff preparation, action item tracking, and initial project documentation. Coordinate project closeout activities, including final records organization, deliverable verification, closeout checklists, lessons learned tracking, and final documentation support. Coordinate and manage assigned project activities in accordance with CAAT policies, procedures, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), templates, and reporting requirements. Coordinate with the Business Operations Manager to ensure project meeting documentation, project records, and related materials are maintained in accordance with CAAT processes. Other duties assigned in support of CAAT operations and Fort Worth-based coordination requirements. Project Controls, Documentation, Reporting, and Meeting Support: 35% Prepare project meeting agendas, meeting notes, action item summaries, decision logs, attendance records, and follow-up trackers for assigned CAAT project meetings. Participate in project meetings, technical interchange meetings, internal coordination meetings, partner meetings, and sponsor-facing meetings to document decisions, action items, risks, issues, and required follow-up. jd_text: Our patients are our number one priority! We're committed to giving children back their childhood! Job Posting Title: Technology Sourcing Specialist Location: Dallas - Hospital Additional Posting Details: Monday - Friday, Days Job Description: Duties/Responsibilities Lead and administer the end-to-end technology sourcing lifecycle, including intake, requirements validation, market research, competitive evaluation, vendor due diligence, negotiation, contracting, implementation handoff, renewal, and termination. Manage TEC operations, including meeting schedules, agendas, materials, decision documentation, action items, approvals, and stakeholder communications. Partner with business and clinical requestors to clarify needs, expected outcomes, funding, timing, alternatives, dependencies, and total cost of ownership. Develop and execute sourcing strategies for software, hardware, cloud services, professional services, maintenance, support, and other technology-related purchases. Coordinate vendor risk, cybersecurity, privacy, architecture, integration, accessibility, compliance, and operational assessments with the appropriate subject-matter experts. Negotiate commercially favorable pricing, terms, service commitments, and protections while maintaining productive vendor relationships. Maintain a centralized inventory of technology agreements, renewal dates, notice periods, financial commitments, ownership, risk findings, and required actions. Monitor contract performance, vendor obligations, service levels, utilization, spend, and stakeholder satisfaction; coordinate corrective actions and escalations when needed. Establish a risk-based vendor governance framework that segments vendors by criticality, spend, data access, operational dependency, and regulatory impact, with oversight requirements appropriate to each tier. Develop and maintain vendor scorecards and lead periodic business reviews that evaluate service levels, quality, responsiveness, security and compliance obligations, financial performance, contractual commitments, and opportunities for improvement. Own vendor issue management and escalation, including root-cause analysis, corrective action plans, service credits, dispute resolution, risk acceptance, and timely communication to accountable stakeholders. Coordinate vendor onboarding, material changes, and offboarding with business owners and control functions, ensuring appropriate access, documentation, knowledge transfer, data return or destruction, asset recovery, and continuity planning. Partner with vendor and internal leaders to maintain relationship plans, product and service roadmaps, executive engagement, innovation opportunities, and succession or exit strategies for critical suppliers. Lead renewal planning far enough in advance to assess value, utilization, alternatives, budget impact, negotiation leverage, and termination requirements. Identify opportunities to consolidate vendors, eliminate redundant technology, improve license utilization, reduce cost, and simplify the technology portfolio. Prepare sourcing analyses, negotiation summaries, status reports, decision briefs, dashboards, and recommendations for leaders and governance committees. Establish and improve sourcing standards, templates, workflows, controls, documentation, and performance measures. Support audits and ensure sourcing records are complete, accurate, accessible, and retained in accordance with organizational requirements. Required Skills/Abilities Bachelor’s degree in business administration, supply chain, information technology, finance, contract management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in technology sourcing, procurement, vendor management, contract management, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience negotiating software, cloud, hardware, professional services, maintenance, and support agreements. Working knowledge of commercial contract terms, licensing models, subscription pricing, service-level agreements, data protection requirements, and vendor risk concepts. Experience coordinating cross-functional reviews with Legal, Information Security, Privacy, Finance, Supply Chain, technical teams, and business stakeholders. Strong analytical, financial, organizational, negotiation, written communication, and presentation skills. Ability to manage multiple complex initiatives, deadlines, stakeholders, and confidential information with limited supervision. Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and experience using contract lifecycle management, procurement, service management, or vendor management platforms. Experience sourcing technology in a healthcare or similarly regulated environment. Knowledge of healthcare privacy, security, and regulatory considerations applicable to technology vendors and hosted services. Experience with enterprise applications, electronic health records, cloud platforms, cybersecurity services, infrastructure, integrations, and software-as-a-service solutions. Professional certification such as Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM), Certified Purchasing Manager (CPM), Certified Commercial Contracts Manager (CCCM), Certified Federal Contracts Manager (CFCM), Certified Professional Contracts Manager (CPCM), or an equivalent credential. Experience implementing or administering contract lifecycle management and vendor performance processes. TAMUK offers the widest range of academic programs and degrees in South Texas, provides exceptional learning and residential facilities, conducts impactful research, awards substantial scholarships, and has awarded more than 80,000 degrees in the institution’s 100-year history. The university is recognized for its unwavering commitment to student success, meaningful research, and deep community engagement. With a welcoming campus culture and strong regional partnerships, TAMUK offers faculty and staff a unique opportunity to make a lasting difference in the lives of students and the broader South Texas region. The position coordinates academic technology operations across classrooms, conference spaces, digital learning environments, and other institutional facilities. Collaborates with academic leadership, the Institutional Facilities Project Manager, Campus Operations, ITS, campus stakeholders, and external partners to plan and implement innovative, accessible, and technology-enabled learning environments. Oversees operational processes and service delivery models, including preventative maintenance, incident response, and technology lifecycle management. Develops, implements, and maintains standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure consistency, compliance, and operational effectiveness. Cultivates collaborative partnerships with campus leadership, Campus Operations, ITS, Event Planning, Facilities, and external vendors to support integrated technology solutions. Strategic Planning, Project Management, and Resource Administration Leads and collaborates in the coordination, prioritization, and execution of work with Campus Operations, establishing service expectations, schedules, and resource allocations. Manages the planning and implementation of academic technology initiatives, including classroom technology upgrades, AV integrations, and emerging technology deployments. Applies formal project management methodologies to define scope, timelines, milestones, risks, and resource requirements, ensuring successful project delivery. Administers budgets in collaboration with Center for Academic Technology leadership and coordinates the procurement, evaluation, selection, and deployment of instructional and AV technologies. Ensures fiscal responsibility, resource optimization, and alignment with institutional priorities and standards. Innovation, Emerging Technologies, and Continuous Improvement Advances the integration and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within academic technology operations, supporting AI-enabled teaching and learning tools, service automation, and data-informed decision-making. Promotes human-centered, ethical, accessible, and compliant AI practices aligned with institutional priorities and emerging higher education trends. Monitors service metrics and implements continuous improvement strategies to enhance operational efficiency and user experience. Promotes ongoing professional development and continuous learning related to emerging technologies, accessibility requirements, AI-enabled teaching and learning, and workforce innovation environments. Identifies and supports innovative solutions that enhance teaching, learning, collaboration, and institutional effectiveness. jd_text: Job Title Business Technology Specialist Agency Tarleton State University Department Continuous Improvement Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Stephenville, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description Tarleton State University, a distinguished Doctoral National Comprehensive University, invites applications for the position of Business Technology Specialist in the Department of Continuous Improvement . From a lively live music scene and numerous local festivals to rich traditions rooted in the surrounding community, Stephenville provides a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere. title: Hazard Mitigation Planning Specialist
jd_text: Job Title Hazard Mitigation Planning Specialist Agency Texas A&M University Department Institute For A Disaster Resilient Texas Proposed Minimum Salary $5,833.34 monthly Job Location College Station, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description Who We Are The Institute for a Disaster Resilient Texas (IDRT) at Texas A&M University brings together research, data, and collaboration to strengthen communities against natural hazards. Established to bridge the gap between science and decision-making, IDRT delivers cutting-edge analytics, tools, and evidence-based solutions that support state agencies, partners, and local communities in preparing for, responding to, and recovering from disasters. Through innovative research and a commitment to public impact, we help build a more resilient Texas for the long term. To learn more, visit https://idrt.tamu.edu What We Want We are seeking a candidate who is an exceptional technical writer, skilled facilitator, and innovative problem solver with expertise in hazard mitigation planning, community resilience, and the development of practical solutions that strengthen disaster preparedness and recovery. What You Need to Know Salary: $70,000 - $80,000/annually. Cover Letter/Resume: A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended and will help in our review. You may upload them on the application under the CV/Resume section. Additional Request: Applicants are encouraged to submit a professional portfolio demonstrating relevant planning, hazard mitigation, GIS, data analysis, or resilience work. Applicants may also include a sample of technical writing they have led or substantially contributed to. Other Requirements and Factors: This position is funded from grant and/or contract funding , which is renewed through provisions of the grantor of the contract. Therefore, this position is contingent upon continuation of funding from these grants and/or contracts, as well as satisfactory job performance. This position may require work beyond normal office hours and/or work on weekends. May travel as required. Essential Duties/Tasks Hazard Mitigation Planning and Technical Writing Development and update of FEMA-compliant Hazard Mitigation Plans. Serve as principal contributor, for planning documents and resilience assessments. Conduct and document hazard identification, vulnerability assessments, and risk analyses. Develop mitigation goals, objectives, and action strategies that support long-term community resilience. Ensure planning products comply with FEMA Mitigation Planning Policy Guide requirements and applicable state and federal standards. Coordinate plan development through stakeholder review, adoption, and FEMA approval. Prepare technical reports, planning documents, white papers, and related deliverables. Stakeholder Engagement and Project Management Facilitate planning committee meetings, workshops, and public engagement activities. Coordinate with local governments, emergency managers, councils of governments, nonprofit organizations, and state and federal agencies. Present project findings and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences. Innovation and Artificial Intelligence Applications Apply AI and advanced analytical tools to support planning, research, technical writing, data analysis, document review, and project management activities. Evaluate emerging technologies that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of resilience planning and applied research. Contribute to the development of best practices for responsible AI use in hazard mitigation and resilience planning. Support training activities related to innovative planning and research methods. Proposal Development and Sponsored Research Support proposal development for federal, state, and private-sector funding opportunities. Assist with project reporting and sponsor deliverables. Contribute to the growth of the Institute's hazard mitigation planning portfolio. Applied Research and Technical Analysis Conduct hazard, vulnerability, resilience, climate, and flood risk assessments. Integrate demographic, environmental, and geospatial datasets into research products. Collaborate with faculty, research scientists, and graduate students on research initiatives. Contribute to the development of innovative approaches to disaster resilience. Qualifications Required Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in urban planning, Emergency Management, Geography, Public Administration, Environmental Science, Engineering, Natural Resources, or a closely related field. Eight years of related experience in hazard mitigation planning, resilience planning, emergency management, climate adaptation, or related field. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in urban planning, Emergency Management, Geography, Public Administration, Environmental Science, Engineering, Natural Resources, or a closely related field. Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM), American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP), Certified Emergency Manager (CEM), and/or related professional certification. 3-year experience serving as a lead author, primary contributor, project manager, or technical lead for FEMA-compliant hazard mitigation plans. 3-year experience of working on FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA), Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP), Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA), Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC), or similar programs. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Ability to effectively utilize a computer and applicable software for technical writing, editing and print production. Ability to utilize Geographic Information System (GIS) and geospatial analysis to support planning and decision-making. Ability to use Python, R, machine learning, large language models, natural language processing, or other advanced analytical methods. Familiarity with using artificial intelligence tools or advanced analytical technologies in professional planning, research, technical writing, data analysis, or project management workflows. Skilled in utilizing various learning and active listening strategies. Ability to orally comprehend and express information and use inductive and deductive reasoning. Ability to positively and professionally interact with clients and staff, groups of various sizes. Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others. Why Texas A&M University? We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes. Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life and AD&D, flexible spending accounts , and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M contributing to employee health and basic life premiums 12-15 days of annual paid holidays Up to eight hours of paid sick leave and at least eight hours of paid vacation each month Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas Health and Wellness: Free exercise programs and release time Professional Development: All employees have access to free LinkedIn Learning training, webinars, and limited financial support to attend conferences, workshops, and more Educational release time and tuition assistance for completing a degree while a Texas A&M employee Living Well, a program at Texas A&M that has been built by employees, for employees Our Commitment Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service. All positions are security-sensitive. jd_text: Job Title Philanthropy System Analyst Agency West Texas A&M University Department Advancement Services Proposed Minimum Salary $4,072.25 monthly Job Location Canyon, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description The A&M System strives to maintain a competitive, high-quality benefit package to support the health and wellness needs of our workforce. This includes comprehensive health and welfare insurance plans, additional health and lifestyle programs, and optional retirement savings opportunities. Eligible employees will have access to paid leave programs in addition to 13-15 paid holidays each year. For more information regarding the benefit package go to: West Texas A&M University: Human Resources Benefits NOTICE - All posted positions are subject to budget approval. General Summary: The Philanthropy System Analyst is responsible for working with others in all areas of the Philanthropy Division as well as with IT to identify operational problems and find solutions. The Philanthropy System Analyst will train users, create reports, conduct user acceptance testing and assist the Philanthropy Team to use the Philanthropy System so it provides the greatest ROI. Responsibilities: Create lists, queries and exports to extract data from the Ascend CRM with specific criteria Work with IT to develop Ascend CRM to meet the needs of philanthropy users and IT Provide user support for Ascend CRM functionality. Test new releases/updates and work with Philanthropy leadership in decision making and implementation of changes. Develop and recommend data integrity and quality audits for the Ascend CRM to ensure the accuracy of data entry and record coding. Develop methods for streamlining data entry and extraction processes within Ascend CRM. Develop and document relevant business processes involving Ascend CRM including a data dictionary, code tables and crosswalks for data that exists across multiple systems Performs regular data appending procedures from a variety of sources (example: NCOA update and email appends, etc.) following best practices Work with Alumni and Annual Giving on appeal standards, tracking appeal performance, etc. This document represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties as assigned. Maintains 100% compliance with timely completion of required System, University and job-specific online training courses. Necessary Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. Four (4) years of related experience. Systems Analyst experience. Working with end users and IT. Knowledge of donor software (example: Raisers Edge, Ascend, Salesforce, etc.). Create lists, queries and exports. Understanding of data administration and management functions. Proficiency in Microsoft Office primary software, particularly Excel for use with data. Ability to train, motivate and communicate with staff in a high-volume goal oriented, friendly work environment. Ability to maintain confidentiality. Ability to learn and effectively use new software. Self-Motivated, self-directed, collegial, creative and results oriented. Must have an advanced ability to prioritize tasks, schedules and objectives. Must be collaborative with a strong commitment to team support and positive customer service. Excellent written and verbal communication skills along with strong interpersonal skills and attention to detail. Technical understanding of CRM database systems. Preferred Qualifications: Master’s degree in computer science or related management field. Eight (8) years of related experience. Experience in developing and maintaining dashboards for displaying and analyzing data. Experience with Ascend, Affinaquest, Salesforce and/or Raisers Edge. Fundraising CRM experience. Applicant Instructions: Please include the following with your application: Cover letter Resume Three references Please attach all documents in the attachment box at the bottom of the “My Experience” page before continuing through the application. Please use the “Upload” button to add each document individually. All revisions must be made prior to application submission. If you need assistance with uploading documents, please contact WTAMU Human Resources at hr@wtamu.edu . Due to budgetary reasons, West Texas A&M University will not offer H-1B or other work authorization visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and maintain work authorization throughout the employment term. Texas law requires all males age 18 through 25 to be properly registered with the Selective Service System. Equal Opportunity /Veterans/Disability Employer. All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check. title: Principal Product Manager, Member Experience
jd_text: Join the team leading the next evolution of virtual care. At Teladoc Health, you are empowered to bring your true self to work while helping millions of people live their healthiest lives. Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens. Summary of Position You'll own the vision and strategy for the core member software experience across the full care journey, from the moment a member first discovers what care is available through getting care and following up afterward. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who thinks in systems, has strong product design sense, and uses data and user research to decide what to build and why. You'll turn ambiguous, cross-cutting problems into clear direction, set a vision that delights members while working within the realities of a complex, regulated healthcare environment, and earn trust with partners from engineering leads to senior executives. You operate with a high degree of autonomy and are the person we point at a complex, high-priority problem to chase down end to end. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Set the vision and strategy: define a multi-year vision and roadmap for the core member-facing software experience across the full care journey, and prioritize smartly among competing efforts to deliver the greatest value for members. Think in systems: map the complete member journey end to end, break down ambiguous, cross-cutting problems into clear requirements, and drive alignment across engineering, design, data science, clinical, operations, and marketing. Champion great design: partner with design as a strategic differentiator, contribute directly to design reviews and critiques, push back where warranted, and hold a high bar on craft and attention to detail, connecting the smallest interaction elements into a coherent end-to-end experience, especially where metrics don't fully capture what members feel. Drive outcomes with data and research: use user research, behavioral data, and A/B testing to inform decisions and pivot or stop work when the evidence demands it; define success metrics, and counter-metrics focused on activation, engagement, retention, and lasting member value. Take ideas from concept to impact: convert opportunities into well-scoped projects, lead the team through prototyping, launch, and iteration, and hold the team to a high standard of execution. Lead up, down, and across the organization: serve as a credible senior product voice with engineers and executives alike, synthesize complexity into a simple, persuasive narrative, create clarity without pretending certainty by communicating what we believe, what we've learned, and what remains unknown, and carry complex conversations independently. Raise the bar for product: mentor other product managers on product craft, systems thinking, and analytical rigor. The time spent on each responsibility reflects an estimate and is subject to change dependent on business needs. Supervisory Responsibilities No Qualifications Expected for Position 12+ years of product management experience at a senior level in consumer-facing products at meaningful scale, with enough breadth and variety of problems to think from first principles. Direct ownership of at least one consumer product experience from ambiguous problem to measurable adoption, with evidence of discovering product direction rather than only delivering against an established roadmap. Strong command of B2C product dynamics, including onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, and habit formation across multi-step user journeys. Strong product analytics proficiency, including experience with product analytics tools and SQL; able to combine qualitative and quantitative insight to make sound decisions with incomplete information, tell signal from noise, and explain what was learned beyond which number moved. Strong technical fluency, including an understanding of how modern software applications work, APIs, data flows, and system dependencies; able to collaborate effectively with engineering and understand technical constraints and trade-offs without requiring deep platform or architectural expertise. Executive presence and a proven ability to build trust with business and engineering stakeholders and to influence senior leaders in a matrixed organization without formal authority. Empathy for users navigating health concerns and genuine conviction about the role technology can play in improving healthcare access and outcomes; experience in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated, high-stakes categories is a plus but not required. Exceptional written and verbal communication; fluency at both altitudes, from articulating a differentiated vision to working through the detailed tradeoffs required to ship it; low ego and high ownership; the judgment to balance collaborative openness with decisive vision-setting, and comfort advocating for a direction among ambiguous options in fast-moving environments where the answer isn't handed to you. Travel: Up to 10% Travel expectations are approximate and subject to change based on business needs. Bonus Qualifications Strong product design sense: fluent in design language, able to give structured, differentiated critique and bring taste and craft to design conversations; experience working in design-forward product organizations. Experience in digital health, health tech, or another high-stakes consumer space preferred. Comfortable operating with high autonomy in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where standards and processes often need to be built from scratch. The base salary range for this position is $200,000 - $230,000. In addition to a base salary, this position is eligible for a performance bonus and benefits (subject to eligibility requirements) listed here: Teladoc Health Benefits 2026 . Total compensation is based on several factors including, but not limited to, type of position, location, education level, work experience, and certifications. This information is applicable for all full-time positions. #LI-SS2 #LI-Remote We follow a Flexible Vacation Policy, intended for rest, relaxation, and personal time. All time off must be approved by your manager prior to use. You will also receive 80 hours of Paid Sick, Safe, and Caregiver Leave annually. This applies to full-time positions only. If you are applying for a part-time role, your recruiter can provide additional details. As part of our hiring process, we verify identity and credentials, conduct interviews (live or video), and screen for fraud or misrepresentation. Applicants who falsify information will be disqualified. Teladoc Health will not sponsor or transfer employment work visas for this position. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future. Why join Teladoc Health? Teladoc Health is transforming how better health happens. Learn how when you join us in pursuit of our impactful mission . Chart your career path with meaningful opportunities that empower you to grow, lead, and make a difference. Join a multi-faceted community that celebrates each colleague’s unique perspective and is focused on continually improving, each and every day. Contribute to an innovative culture where fresh ideas are valued as we increase access to care in new ways. Enjoy an inclusive benefits program centered around you and your family, with tailored programs that address your unique needs. Explore candidate resources with tips and tricks from Teladoc Health recruiters and learn more about our company culture by exploring #TeamTeladocHealth on LinkedIn . As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we never have and never will discriminate against any job candidate or employee due to age, race, religion, color, ethnicity, national origin, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, membership in an employee organization, medical condition, family history, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, parental status, or pregnancy). In our innovative and inclusive workplace, we prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. In furtherance of your employment relationship with Teladoc Health, we collect personal information responsibly and in accordance with applicable data privacy laws, including but not limited to, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). title: Sr. Manager, Data Scientist, Marketing Analytics
jd_text: Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period! For more information about our benefits, see below! We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet." Overview We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Sr. Manager, Data Scientist to lead a team of talented data scientists focused on advancing our marketing analytics capabilities. This role will be instrumental in translating complex marketing challenges into data-driven solutions, driving insights that optimize campaign performance, enhance customer understanding, and maximize ROI. The ideal candidate will possess a strong blend of technical expertise in data science, proven leadership abilities, and a deep understanding of marketing strategies and analytics. Duties & Responsibilities Team Leadership & Management Lead, mentor, and develop a team of 2-3 data scientists, fostering a collaborative and high-performing environment. Set clear goals, provide regular feedback, and conduct performance reviews for team members. Support the professional growth of team members through training, conferences, and challenging assignments. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify opportunities for leveraging data science to create business value. Manage competing priorities across multiple projects while ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards. Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of data science projects, from ideation and prototyping to production and monitoring. Conduct rigorous reviews of statistical and optimization models to ensure they meet business needs, technical standards, and ethical guidelines. Executive Presence including excellent communication and presentation skills, written and verbal and ability to communicate at all levels within large organizations. Technical Execution & Innovation Apply a strong understanding of statistical modeling, machine learning algorithms, and experimental design. Oversee the end-to-end data science lifecycle, including data collection, cleaning, feature engineering, model development, validation, deployment, and monitoring. Ensure the integrity and accuracy of data used for analysis and modeling. Contribute to the development of scalable data pipelines and analytical infrastructure in collaboration with data engineering teams. Hands-on experience deploying models from development through production in a modern data science stack Champion the use of cutting-edge data science techniques to solve challenging marketing problems. Strategic Marketing Analytics & Insights Partner closely with marketing leadership and stakeholders to understand business objectives and identify opportunities for data science to drive impact. Define and execute the roadmap for marketing analytics initiatives, aligning with overall business strategy. Lead the design, development, and implementation of advanced analytical models (e.g., attribution modeling, customer lifetime value (CLTV),, segmentation, propensity modeling, personalization algorithms, media mix modeling (MMM)). Develop and implement A/B and multivariate testing frameworks and methodologies to measure the impact of marketing initiatives. Stay abreast of industry trends and emerging technologies in data science and marketing analytics. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams including Marketing, Product, Sales, IT, and Data Engineering. Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for marketing teams and senior leadership. Act as a subject matter expert in data science and marketing analytics within the organization. Education Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field. Experience 10+ years of progressive experience in data science, with at least 2-3 years in a leadership or management role, leading a team of data scientists. Extensive experience with ML predictive analytics, optimization algorithms, and large-scale data processing frameworks. Significant experience working in cross-functional teams and influencing stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Demonstrable experience with many of the following: Demand Forecasting, Segmentation, Testing, Predictive Customer Response, Price Optimization, Marketing Mix Modeling, Customer Journey Analytics, Next Best Product/Offer, Customer Elasticity (Market Response Modeling), Skills & Competencies Expert proficiency in Python (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch) and/or R. Strong SQL skills for data extraction and manipulation. Experience with big data technologies (e.g., Spark, Hadoop) and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure). Solid understanding of statistical inference, experimental design, and causal analysis. Proven ability to build, deploy, and monitor machine learning models in production environments. Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels. Strong problem-solving abilities and a strategic mindset. No sponsorship or OPT available Base Pay Range $135,700 - $176,400 / year While starting pay falls within the given range, it can vary based on factors like geographic location, skills, education, and experience. Total earnings may also be affected by overtime, incentives, commissions, performance, and route assignment (where applicable). #LI-Remote Why Choose Us? A career with the Rentokil family of companies can be a professional trajectory filled with opportunity. We pride ourselves on being a world-class team that rewards high performance, and we love to promote from within. We offer competitive pay and many of our roles offer performance incentives. Below you'll find information about some of what we have to offer. All Full-Time Colleagues qualify for the following and Part-Time Colleagues qualify for most benefits after they meet certain criteria. Click here to read more about our Total Rewards Program which includes: Professional and Personal Growth Multiple avenues to grow your career Training and development programs available Tuition Reimbursement benefits (for FT Colleagues) Health and Wellness Full-time colleagues are eligible to begin enrollment immediately upon hire with benefits starting on day 1 Health benefits including Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, and Life Insurance plus much more Savings and Retirement 401(k) retirement plan with company-matching contributions Work-Life Balance Vacation days & sick days Company-paid holidays & floating holidays A company mindset that prioritizes health, safety, and flexibility We are looking for individuals who want to make a difference where our customers live and work. Is that you? This company is a Drug Free workplace. Rentokil is committed to complying with all Federal, State, and local laws related to the employment of qualified individuals with disabilities. title: Financial Systems Senior Analyst
jd_text: Texas Capital is built to help businesses and their leaders. Our depth of knowledge and expertise allows us to bring the best of the big firms at a scale that works for our clients, with highly experienced bankers who truly invest in people’s success — today and tomorrow. While we are rooted in core financial products, we are differentiated by our approach. Our bankers are seasoned financial experts who possess deep experience across a multitude of industries. Equally important, they bring commitment — investing the time and resources to understand our clients’ immediate needs, identify market opportunities and meet long-term objectives . At Texas Capital, we do more than build business success. We build long-lasting relationships. Texas Capital provides a variety of benefits to colleagues, including health insurance coverage, wellness program, fertility and family building aids, life and disability insurance, retirement savings plans with a generous 401K match, paid leave programs, paid holidays, and paid time off (PTO). Headquartered in Dallas with offices in Austin, Fort Worth, Houston, Richardson, Plano and San Antonio, Texas Capital was recently named Best Regional Bank in 2024 by Bankrate and was named to The Dallas Morning News ’ Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex Top Workplaces 2023 and GoBankingRate’s 2023 list of Best Regional Banks. For more information about joining our team, please visit us at www.texascapitalbank.com . Overview This Financial Systems Senior Analyst role is a vital member of the Enterprise Business Management (EBM) Office that provides direct oversight of enterprise finance platforms and data workflows across Texas Capital Bank. This high-profile role combines data integration expertise with platform governance in support of the EBM Office's expanding charter. The position provides opportunities to work directly with finance, technology, and business leadership in designing data flows, managing platform configurations, and ensuring data usability across downstream systems. This role has a strong systems and data focus and will require a self-motivated, action-oriented strategic thinker who can prioritize, communicate, and collaborate to build relationships across departmental lines and drive platform initiatives to successful completion. Responsibilities · Be a key partner to the Enterprise Finance Leadership Team; supporting enterprise business management capabilities across several models, projects and their reporting in Apptio. · Design and document data flow architecture; identify integration points, data dependencies, and handoff sequences. · Establish data mapping standards and master data governance across platforms to ensure consistency in definitions, hierarchies, and dimensions. · Contribute to the development of data governance policies and practices for platforms facilitated by the EBM Office. · Support the establishment of data quality standards, validation rules, and remediation workflows; track SLAs for data completeness, accuracy, and timeliness. · Document platform capabilities, data schemas, and business rules; maintain current documentation of platform configuration and data lineage. · Identify manual processes and redundant data entry across finance systems; design and implement automated workflows to reduce rework and improve timeliness. · Act as a liaison between the EBM Office, Corporate Finance, IT, and business units on platform, data, and allocation matters. · Monitor data integration health, latency, and quality; proactively identify and resolve integration failures or data anomalies. Requirements · An undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Finance, or related field. · A minimum of 5 years of related experience in data integration, ETL, data governance, or enterprise systems administration. · Initiative to identify data quality issues, scope and logically structure an analysis, extract relevant insights, and communicate with a point of view. · Strong technical foundation: SQL, relational databases, and data modeling; ability to read and interpret technical documentation. · Expertise in data governance frameworks, master data management, or information architecture. · Problem solver attitude with a curious mindset. · Self-motivated, results-oriented self-starter. · Ability to build relationships with, and provide thought leadership to, officers of TCB. · Experience thriving in a dynamic and fast-moving work environment. · Experience effectively managing several work streams and projects concurrently. · Superior analytical skills and attention to detail. · Strong communication (written and oral) and partnering skills. · Strong PC skills, including proficiency in Excel and experience sourcing data from database applications. Preferred · Familiarity with Apptio or relevant platform data models. · Experience with technology business management (TBM), enterprise business management (EBM), financial planning and analysis (FP&A), or enterprise finance. · Hands-on experience with ETL tools (e.g., Informatica, Talend, MuleSoft) or API-based integration patterns. · Experience with data governance tools or metadata management platforms. · Prior experience supporting a technology organization. · Certification in ITSM, data management, governance, or relevant platform (e.g., Apptio Training). · MBA/MIS or similar degree/certification. The duties listed above are the essential functions, or fundamental duties within the job classification. The essential functions of individual positions within the classification may differ. Texas Capital Bank may assign reasonably related additional duties to individual employees consistent with standard departmental policy.Texas Capital is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jd_text: Your Opportunity as the Senior Manager, Retail Operations This role leads the strategy, governance, and execution model for national retail coverage across J.M. Smucker Company priorities. This position is accountable for strengthening the company’s partnership with Acosta and other retail partners, improving the effectiveness of the retail coverage model, increasing accountability for retail investment, and ensuring retail activity translates into measurable business value. The role connects retail execution, customer priorities, display management, reporting, financial governance, and data-led on-shelf availability. Working across Sales, Procurement, Finance, Deduction Management, Transportation, category teams, external broker partners, and customer-facing teams, this leader establishes clear processes, improves execution, and directs resources toward the highest-value opportunities. Location: Working Remote, USA and residing near a major airport Work Arrangements: Approximate travel 50% or as business needs require. In this role you will: Lead Retail Operations strategy and execution. · Develop and continuously refine the national retail broker model across Food and Beverage, Hostess, convenience, and other priority retail channels, including dedicated and syndicated coverage, convenience-store support, back-office support, and customer-specific retail programs. · Set retail execution strategy across selling, merchandising, distribution correction, promotional execution, in-aisle activity, secondary displays, and total-company display execution. · Prioritize retail resources using account-level needs, store productivity, execution requirements, and expected return. · Support Perfect Store, 360 Selling, seasonal limited-time offers, shipper deployment, display management, and customer-specific execution initiatives. Strengthen retail partner governance and accountability. · Serve as a primary point of contact for Acosta and other retail partner relationships, ensuring activities, coverage levels, costs, and expected outcomes are clearly defined. · Lead scorecards, monthly and quarterly business reviews, customer coverage reviews, and recurring performance discussions that connect field activity with customer priorities and measurable business results. · Challenge coverage levels and redirect resources when productivity, execution requirements, or expected return do not support the investment. · Partner with Procurement, Finance, Sales, and Deduction Management to define broker services, negotiate appropriate rates, validate billing, monitor variances, and connect costs with services delivered. Advance data-led retail execution and on-shelf availability. · Use customer-specific data, Circana insights, real-time out-of-stock scanning, and authorized-item reporting to identify high-value distribution and availability opportunities before representatives enter stores. · Translate alerts, scorecards, and key performance indicator reporting into actionable priorities for retail representatives and sales teams. · Support customer initiatives such as Kroger On-Shelf Availability by connecting store-level corrections with customer ordering processes and broader retail productivity goals. · Measure execution impact across store visits, out-of-stocks, void correction, cases influenced, cases packed out, display execution, and priority-program performance. Improve planning discipline and field communication. · Drive earlier communication among Sales, Retail Operations, customers, and broker partners to improve execution windows, reset readiness, and store-level awareness. · Establish recurring customer coverage reviews focused on shipment and key performance indicator tracking, planogram compliance, retail tools, and 90-day retail planning calendars. · Facilitate ad hoc requests from internal sales teams, field teams, and category partners while ensuring ownership and priorities are clear. · Lead internal share-out meetings to communicate progress, risks, opportunities, and required follow-up actions. Manage display, freight, and retail investment governance. · Maintain oversight of the Hostess display-management relationship, budget, ordering, deployment, inventory, and shipment planning. · Establish disciplined financial review, return-on-investment evaluation, and approval processes before deploying display equipment or retail resources. · Identify opportunities for cost avoidance, improved financial control, reduced freight exposure, and stronger accountability for retail investment. Lead cross-functional problem solving and process improvement. · Coordinate Sales priorities, field execution, Procurement discussions, Finance requirements, deduction-management needs, display production, analytics, transportation considerations, and customer-specific requirements. · Diagnose execution challenges by identifying whether root causes involve coverage, communication, inventory, reporting, store authorization, timing, ownership, or process gaps. · Partner with Pet and other counterpart teams to develop standard operating procedures, best practices, execution strategies, and consistent ways of working. What we are looking for: Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree. 10+ years of experience in consumer packaged goods (CPG), retail operations, sales strategy, customer execution, broker management, or related commercial roles. Experience directing a national retail agency or broker partner and managing retail coverage models, services, costs, billing, resource allocation, scorecards, and performance reviews. Strong knowledge of retail management, broker operations, customer execution, store-level merchandising, planograms, display and promotional execution, distribution correction, and on-shelf availability. Experience translating customer, syndicated, store-level, and operational data into field priorities, measurable outcomes, and practical actions. Strong commercial and financial acumen, including evaluating retail investments and prioritizing resources based on customer needs, productivity, execution requirements, and expected return. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes and create clear operating processes that connect field activity, customer priorities, reporting, and financial governance. Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives and working effectively across Sales, Procurement, Finance, Deduction Management, Transportation, category and analytics teams, external partners, and customer-facing organizations. Strong communication, facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, including the ability to establish accountability and influence senior leaders without direct authority. Ability to lead through ambiguity, make sound decisions, balance immediate execution with long-term operating-model improvements, and create effective planning, governance, and executive-update routines. Additional skills and experience that we think would make someone successful in this role: Master of Business Administration, other relevant advanced degree, or certification in retail analytics, project management, process improvement, or financial management. Experience working with Acosta, Advantage Solutions, or a comparable national retail agency across food, beverage, convenience, or other consumer packaged goods retail channels. Experience with Perfect Store, 360 Selling, seasonal programs, display deployment, planogram compliance, and on-shelf availability initiatives. Experience overseeing display management, freight, deduction management, or related retail investment processes. Experience using customer-specific, Circana, authorized-item, out-of-stock, or comparable retail analytics tools. #LI-MR1 The Right Place for You We are bold, kind, strive to do the right thing, we play to win, and we believe in a strong community that thrives together. Our culture is rooted in our Basic Beliefs , and we believe in supporting every employee by meeting their physical, emotional, and financial needs. Stay connected with us on LinkedIn® We're an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, age, national origin, disability status or protected veteran status.

title: CRA Credit & Investment Business Strategy Manager
location: Remote Opportunity - VA, NC, SC, GA,  FL, AL, TX, & CO
jd_text: The SouthState story is one of steady growth, deep community roots, and an unwavering commitment to helping our customers move forward. Since our beginnings in the 1930s to becoming a trusted financial partner across the South and beyond - we are known for combining personal relationships with forward-thinking solutions. We are committed to helping our team members find their success while maintaining the integrity of our values: building trust, fostering lasting relationships and pursuing excellence. At SouthState, individual contributions are recognized, potential is cultivated and team members are inspired to achieve their greater purpose. Your future begins here! Summary The CRA Credit & Investment Business Strategy Manager is responsible for developing and implementing long-term community development credit and investment strategies that drive growth throughout the Bank’s Assessment Areas, in congruence with the Bank’s goals and objectives. The CRA Credit & Investment Business Strategy Manager will assess CRA credit and investment opportunities aligned with both CRA/Community Development and Bank Strategic goals; to include underwriting and transaction structuring, documenting and lead underwriting and due diligence for qualifying CRA investments such as LIHTC, NMTC, EQ2, SBIC, and others. The CRA Credit & Investment Business Strategy Manager will balance the Banks strategic goals, Community Engagement mission impact, profitability, policy and risk. The CRA Credit & Investment Business Strategy Manager will act as the internal CRA advocate in collaboration with internal business line partners, external partners to include investors, developers, vendors, and others as necessary. Duties & Responsibilities Work with Senior Leadership, CRA Investment Working Group, Director of Community Engagement, Director of Corporate Stewardship and others (i.e. CD Officers, Local Leadership) to create and deploy strategies in collaboration with stakeholders efforts surrounding enhancing community development lending and investments. Organizational alignment and cross-functional collaboration – align with various business lines, (Credit, Small Business, Commercial, Retail, Mortgage, ERM, MarCom, Corporate Stewardship etc.) and Regional & Community Leadership on local needs and incorporating local relationships with a Community Development focus. Includes supporting the various local leadership in investment opportunities and understanding resources required to implement new Community Development loans and investment initiatives in their local community. Takes initiative to lead and successfully supports and defends communities needs for new community development loans and investments to include both commercial and mortgage related transactions , i.e. LIHTC, NMTC, EQ2, down payment assistance programs, mortgage-backed securities etc. Conduct or support commercial and community development credit underwriting, including analysis of borrower/guarantor financial statements, cash flow, collateral, repayment sources, global debt capacity, and risk factors. Not with the intent to approve the transaction, but advocate for approval by local leadership and credit team. Evaluate, structure, and recommend community development loans and investments consistent with CRA objectives, credit policy, and risk appetite. Includes due diligence on opportunities including but not limited to LIHTC, NMTC, EQ2, loan funds, CDFI related credit extensions, and securitized investments as applicable. Prepare or contribute to credit memos, investment summaries, approval packages, and portfolio monitoring materials. Collaborate with internal partners (i.e. Credit, Finance, Risk, CRA Investment Working Group, CD Officers, and line of business leaders) to assess transaction structure, policy compliance, risk appetite, and community development eligibility. Monitor performance, covenant compliance, and impact/results of community development credit and investments. Identify and mitigate transaction, credit, operational, compliance and strategic risk associated with loans and investments. Analyze data and prepare risk assessment and mitigation efforts for new and on-going Community Development Loans and Investments. Engage stakeholders both internally and externally through various means of communication, planning, networking, volunteering, etc. to ensure plans and ideas are aligned to support both the Bank’s vision and the community’s needs. Present opportunities to drive Community Development Loan and Investment growth and build Meaningful and Lasting Relationships. It is the responsibility of this role to take ownership of all tasks and challenges that they encounter in the operation of their assigned position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Qualifications Education Requirements Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent work experience. Minimum Experience 8+ years of experience in CRA/Community Development finance, commercial credit, underwriting, lending, and/or community development investments. Demonstrated experience evaluating community development loans, tax credit investments, structured finance, or securitized investment products. Experience partnering with credit/risk/legal/compliance/business line stakeholders in transaction execution. Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities Must have experience in commercial credit analysis and underwriting non-profit and community development financing structures. Must have experience in financial statement spreading and cash flow analysis, credit risk assessment and risk rating concepts. Must have experience with structuring and conduct due diligence on complex community development lending facilities such as LIHTC, NMTC, EQ2, and others. Experience and knowledge of securitized community development investment vehicles and related risk considerations. Ability to conduct due diligence for securitized community development investments. Ability to synthesize financial, community impacts, and regulatory factors into business line and leadership recommendations. Maintain strong knowledge of the Community Reinvestment Act and Fair Lending Laws and regulations. Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to prepare reports and presentations are required. Willingness to collaborate with a strong ability to work across business lines, high emotional intelligence, adaptable to change, able to pivot and ability to exercise discretion. Requires the ability to effectively manage workflow and assignments, appropriate prioritizing work. Attention to detail and accuracy is necessary. Requires the ability to work well with diverse work groups, team and group-oriented activities. Expertise in stakeholder engagement, partnership development, and cross-functional development. Demonstrated success in quantifying community development impact and leveraging data to tell compelling stories. Deep commitment to the Bank’s Core Values and understands the value of storytelling. Physical Demands and Work Environment Physical Demands Ability to communicate in person, on the phone, and through electronic channels Ability to use a computer on a frequent basis, including typing and sustained attention to a monitor Ability to sit, walk, and/or stand for extended periods of time Ability to bend and reach Work Environment Office: If the position reports to a physical Company location, the setting will be a typical office environment. Remote or hybrid: For remote or hybrid positions, a secure and distraction-free setting is required, with a reliable internet connection (cable or fiber preferred, mobile hotspots not acceptable). Hybrid positions will report to a physical Company location, as directed by the manager, and that setting will be a typical office environment. In accordance with Colorado and Virginia law: Pay for this position is anticipated to be between $101,718.00 - $162,484.00 , actual offers to be determined based on applicant’s skills, experience and education. While the anticipated deadline for the job posting is 09-26-2026, we encourage you to submit your application as we may still consider qualified candidates beyond this date. Benefits | SouthState Careers Equal Opportunity Employer, including disabled/veterans.

location: Remote Opportunity - VA, NC, SC, GA,  FL, AL, TX, & CO
jd_text: The SouthState story is one of steady growth, deep community roots, and an unwavering commitment to helping our customers move forward. Since our beginnings in the 1930s to becoming a trusted financial partner across the South and beyond - we are known for combining personal relationships with forward-thinking solutions. We are committed to helping our team members find their success while maintaining the integrity of our values: building trust, fostering lasting relationships and pursuing excellence. At SouthState, individual contributions are recognized, potential is cultivated and team members are inspired to achieve their greater purpose. Your future begins here! Summary The FIU Fraud Data Analyst is responsible for using data, investigative judgment, and fraud analytics to identify, investigate, and mitigate internal and external financial crime risks against the Bank. This role analyzes large and complex datasets, fraud alerts, customer and transaction activity, and emerging fraud trends to support timely risk-based decisions, reduce fraud losses, strengthen controls, and ensure regulatory expectations are met. The position partners with FIU leadership, Fraud Operations, Digital Banking, Treasury Management, Information Technology, Information Security, Compliance, and other business partners to develop actionable insights, improve fraud detection strategies, and support effective reporting and escalation. It is the policy of SouthState Bank to comply with the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), USA PATRIOT Act, and the requirements of the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), and other related anti-money laundering/ anti-terrorist financing initiatives. The Bank has established a Bank Secrecy Act/ Anti-Money Laundering/Office of Foreign Assets Control (BSA/AML/OFAC) Compliance Program, covering all requirements of the BSA, USA PATRIOT Act and OFAC rules and regulations. Upon completion of required training, the Board of Directors of SouthState Bank shall hold each employee accountable for adhering to the established operating procedures and internal controls as set forth in the Bank’s BSA/AML/OFAC Program. Continued instances of non-compliance or willful violation of law may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination. Duties & Responsibilities Evaluate fraud detection rules, monitoring logic, alert performance, false positives, and data quality issues; recommend enhancements to improve detection effectiveness and operational efficiency Develop, maintain, and enhance dashboards, recurring reports, trend analyses, and ad hoc data views to identify fraud patterns, emerging typologies, control gaps, and loss exposure Identify emerging fraud trends, attack patterns, mule activity, account takeover indicators, synthetic identity concerns, suspicious online account opening activity, social engineering indicators, and other financial crime risks Query, extract, validate, and analyze large datasets using SQL-based databases, Snowflake, Excel, and other approved analytical tools to support fraud investigations and strategy development Analyze fraud alerts, account activity, customer behavior, transaction patterns, and other data sources to identify unusual, suspicious, or potentially fraudulent activity Research and analyze high-risk transactions across payment channels, including digital banking, Zelle, Bill Pay, Bank-to-Bank transfers, debit card, wires, ACH, checks, and other products as applicable Communicate internal control deficiencies, data limitations, system issues, and fraud vulnerabilities identified during analytical or investigative work Provide analytical support, peer guidance, training, and subject matter expertise to team members as needed It is the responsibility of this role to take ownership of all tasks and challenges that they encounter in the operation of their assigned position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Qualifications Education Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Finance, Accounting, Criminal Justice, Business, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field preferred. Equivalent related experience may be considered. title: Area Credit Manager
jd_text: Position Purpose: The Area Credit Manager role at SRS exists to safeguard and expedite recovery of the company's assigned account receivable portfolio, under the oversight of the Regional Credit Manager. The incumbent will handle collection calls, customer account reviews, provide guidance on account status to internal teams, process credit applications and job accounts, while also maintaining diligent notes on clients within the company system. This role also necessitates strategic collaboration with both internal and external stakeholders, and involves direct training for progression into a Regional Credit Manager role, strengthening the company's overall financial management practices. Key Responsibilities: Oversee and manage the company's accounts receivable portfolio, ensuring timely collection and safeguarding of assets, under direction from the Regional Credit Manager and the Director of Credit. Make consistent collection calls on due and overdue accounts receivable, documenting each interaction within the company's digital systems for record keeping and company-wide transparency. Regularly review and release orders from ticket holds after careful evaluation. Process and approve credit applications, extending and maintaining credit lines within authority level. Provide continuous oversight of lien and bond rights, requiring thorough knowledge of notices, mechanics liens, and bond claim processes to ensure collection of job balances. Communicate proactively with both internal and external clients, including the sales team and management, to ensure clear understanding of account statuses, credit applications, and company's credit policy. Conduct thorough customer account reviews, providing recommendations on account handling to internal stakeholders as necessary. Track and reconcile any deductions, overseeing joint-check payments and enforcing company credit policy consistently. Participate fully in credit team meetings, learning from interactions and regularly contributing to department-wide discussions for continuous improvement. Direct Manager Direct Reports: The Area Credit Manager at SRS reports directly to the Regional Credit Manager and/or the Director of Credit. The manager utilizes these key supervisory relationships to formulate decisions on credit lines, lien enforcement, and credit policy, while also seeking guidance for continued professional development towards a Regional Credit Manager role. This position does not oversee any direct reports as it is largely independent, although the manager is expected to engage actively and routinely with the Sales team and the Credit team. The successful execution of this role involves comprehensive communication skills, dedicated teamwork with peers, and accurate and timely reporting to superiors. Despite having no direct managerial responsibilities, the Area Credit Manager is required to guide and educate others, including Sales team and customers. They are also expected to uphold the highest standards of credit policy enforcement and provide valuable input in credit team meetings and key performance indicator reviews, ensuring the smooth running of the Company's overall financial operations. Travel Requirements: The Area Credit Manager's role at SRS necessitates domestic travel, primarily for in-person meetings with regional teams, customer visits, or important company events, as directed by the Regional Credit Manager and/or Director of Credit. Physical Requirements: The Area Credit Manager role at SRS generally operates in a professional office environment and as such requires the ability to use standard office equipment such as computers and phones. The ability to remain stationary for extended periods of time, intermittently stand, walk, bend, reach, and perform manual tasks, such as filing or lifting up to 20 pounds, is expected in regular office operations. Good visual acuity and proficiency in reading, writing, and communicating effectively in English is necessary for the satisfactory completion of the essential functions of this position. As an employer committed to ADA principles, the Company is prepared to make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. While performing the duties of this job, reasonable accommodations may include adjustment of the workspace, modifying material or presentations, providing additional technology aids or offering flexibility in work schedule to enable the performance of essential job functions. We encourage candidates to discuss potential accommodations with us and assure that all discussions related to accommodations will remain confidential. At the Company, it is our policy to treat all employees and job applicants fairly and without regard to physical abilities. We aim to maintain a work environment that is inclusive and respectful to all, reinforcing our commitment to equal opportunities. We appreciate your interest in the Area Credit Manager role and look forward to receiving your application. Working Conditions: As the Area Credit Manager at SRS, you will operate in a hybrid environment; remote work is standard with local travel to branches and infrequent air travel for Credit or corporate meetings. This role is characterized by a fast-paced, deadline-driven atmosphere that requires diligence and high levels of concentration. You will find yourself working closely alongside various team members, including the Regional Credit Manager and the Director of Credit, escalating matters to them as necessary. You will also have regular interaction with internal and external customers, calling for exceptional interpersonal and communication skills. Additionally, this role requires a substantial amount of time spent on computer-related activities such as processing credit applications, reviewing account information, maintaining notes and tracking deductions. You will be expected to monitor critical deadlines related to Notices, mechanics' liens, and bond claims, requiring a high level of organization and attention to detail.
