Strong verbal and written communication skills. Who We Are The Education Abroad Office supports Texas A&M University’s commitment to develop global leaders through transformational opportunities abroad. We engage students, faculty and staff to participate in high quality international experiences. Studying abroad encompasses a variety of international experiences including study, research, internships, volunteer opportunities and service learning programs. Study abroad opportunities are available for all students, freshmen through Ph.D. candidates. The various types of study abroad programs can be as short as a week or as long as an academic year. Students can be in a large group or study on an individual program. Programs through the Education Abroad Office help broaden students’ intellectual and personal horizons, help them navigate in different environments, practice or perfect a language, and build a resume to help broaden career options. Why Texas A&M University? We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes. Summary / Mission The Information Security Director leads the enterprise Data Protection, Security Architecture, and Third-Party Cyber Risk Management functions. This role owns the operating model and outcomes for protecting sensitive data across on-prem, cloud, and endpoint environments; directs a team of security architects that define and govern security architecture standards and technology reviews; and runs a scalable vendor due diligence and contract-security requirements program with clear governance and exception handling. The role also partners closely with the Incident Response (IR) team to ensure preparedness, clear reporting obligations, and effective response execution across internal and third-party events. Reporting line & scope Reports to: CISO Teams / functions owned: Data Protection (classification, DLP, encryption, data handling rules, monitoring/response workflows) across endpoint, cloud, and on-prem.(2) Security Architecture (enterprise security architecture blueprint, patterns/standards, architecture reviews for new technologies). Third-Party Cyber Risk (vendor security due diligence, ongoing monitoring, security addendum/contract requirements, exception governance). 3rd Party Cyber Incident Response (operational oversight/enablement; define requirements, playbooks, testing, coordination across teams and vendors). Key responsibilities 1) Data protection program leadership (on-prem, cloud, endpoint) Own the enterprise data protection strategy and operating model , including classification/labeling, handling rules, DLP, and measurable enforcement outcomes. Establish a sustainable classification approach (e.g., small, understandable taxonomy tied to handling expectations and controls) and ensure governance/ownership remains active over time. Implement a phased enforcement approach for DLP (visibility → user education → controlled override → targeted enforcement) to reduce false positives and operational friction. Define exception processes, review cadence, and tuning workflows so data protection does not become “set-and-forget” shelfware. Partner with IT, risk, privacy, legal, compliance, and business data owners to align protection controls to real data flows and regulatory expectations. 2) Security architecture leadership Lead a team of security architects responsible for the security architecture blueprint , including reference architectures, control standards, and reusable patterns. Run architecture reviews for new technologies and major changes, ensuring security requirements are measurable and implementable (and exceptions are formally governed). Ensure security architecture integrates with enterprise platforms (IAM, logging/monitoring, endpoint security, cloud controls) and supports delivery velocity with clear guardrails. 3) Third-party cyber risk management & due diligence Own the end-to-end vendor security assessment lifecycle: intake, risk tiering, due diligence, remediation tracking, risk acceptance, and renewal/continuous monitoring. Establish/maintain a standardized third-party security addendum and baseline contractual security requirements (with deviations handled via a formal, risk-based exception process). Ensure vendor security requirements are specific and enforceable (e.g., defined incident reporting timelines, audit rights, and consequences of non-compliance). 4) 3rd Party Cyber Incident response (IR) oversight and preparedness Ensure incident response capabilities are defined, tested, and integrated across internal teams and third parties, including escalation, containment, recovery, and post-incident corrective actions. Ensure contractual obligations support response needs (e.g., notification windows, root-cause analysis and corrective action expectations for vendors). Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering or related field 10+ years in information security, including leadership over at least two of: data protection/DLP, security architecture, third-party risk, incident response. Experience building governance-driven security programs that balance control enforcement with operational adoption. Demonstrated ability to create measurable, enforceable vendor security requirements and manage exceptions via risk-based governance. Experience operationalizing vendor risk lifecycle activities (tiering, due diligence, remediation, acceptance, continuous monitoring). Strong stakeholder management across legal, privacy, compliance, IT, procurement, and business leadership. Experience implementing a sustainable data protection model (labels/classification + DLP tuning and rollout). Experience managing 3rd party cybersecurity risk program including due diligence, contract language, ongoing monitoring, and incident response. Cloud security architecture experience (major cloud provider environments) and endpoint data controls integration. Job Description The IT Control Testing Senior Analyst is responsible for executing independent risk-based assessments of technology and cybersecurity controls within the Second Line of Defense (2LOD). This role evaluates the design and operating effectiveness of key technology controls, including IT General Controls (ITGCs), IT Application Controls (ITACs), automated controls, and cybersecurity controls, and assesses the associated risk implications of control deficiencies. The role partners closely with Technology, Information Security, Operational Risk, Compliance, and Internal Audit stakeholders to strengthen the organization's risk and control environment. Responsibilities IT Regulatory Compliance & Alignment: Evaluate industry standards, regulatory mandates, and legal requirements relevant to technology and information security. Technology Control Testing & Assurance: Execute independent testing of ITGCs, ITACs, automated controls, and cybersecurity controls. Technology Risk Assessment & Analysis: Evaluate control effectiveness in mitigating technology, cyber, operational, regulatory, and data risks. Assess deficiencies for severity, root cause, residual risk exposure, and business impact. Identify emerging risks and systemic control weaknesses. Second Line of Defense Oversight & Challenge: Provide independent oversight and effective challenge to First Line of Defense stakeholders regarding control design, implementation, testing results, remediation plans, and risk treatment decisions. Issue Management & Remediation Oversight: Review management action plans, validate corrective actions, challenge closure requests when evidence is insufficient, and ensure remediation addresses root causes and risk exposure. o Reporting & Risk Communication: Prepare testing reports, risk assessments, management summaries, and executive reporting. Clearly articulate risk implications and recommendations to stakeholders and governance committees. o Regulatory, Audit & Framework Alignment: Ensure testing activities align with NIST, COBIT, COSO, FFIEC guidance, SOX expectations, and internal risk management frameworks. o Continuous Improvement: Enhance testing methodologies, reporting capabilities, standards, and quality assurance practices to improve technology risk management maturity. Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Business, Accounting, or related discipline. Demonstrated experience performing independent testing of ITGCs, ITACs, automated controls, and cybersecurity controls. Strong knowledge of NIST CSF, COBIT, COSO, FFIEC guidance, and SOX IT control principles. Experience assessing control deficiencies, residual risk, and business impacts. Experience testing controls related to Access Management, Change Management, SDLC, Technology Operations, Application Security, Data Governance, or Cloud Technologies. Strong analytical, critical thinking, communication, and executive reporting skills. Banking or financial services experience preferred. CISA, CRISC, CISSP, CISM, or CIA certifications preferred. title: Administrative Coordinator for CDO Operations & Data
jd_text: Job Posting Location: Claremont, CA Job Posting Title: Administrative Coordinator for CDO Operations & Data Job Description: ABOUT POMONA COLLEGE: Located near Los Angeles, California, Pomona College is widely regarded as one of the nation's premier liberal arts colleges. Established in 1887, Pomona College is known for small classes, a challenging curriculum, close relationships between students and faculty, and a range of student research and leadership opportunities. Pomona is a member of The Claremont Colleges. JOB PURPOSE: The Administrative Coordinator for CDO Operations & Data plays a central role in supporting the operations, administration, and assessment efforts of the Career Development Office (CDO). This position provides high-level administrative support to the Senior Director, manages the logistics and execution of the office's major events and programs, and oversees key financial and operational processes. The Administrative Coordinator also supports the CDO's data-informed approach to student services by collecting, analyzing, and reporting on qualitative and quantitative data. This includes conducting research, benchmarking peer institutions, developing reports and dashboards, and translating data into actionable insights that inform decision-making and demonstrate the impact of the office's programs and services. Success in this role requires the ability to think strategically across all functions of the CDO, connect operational activities to broader departmental goals, and present complex information in clear, accessible formats for a variety of audiences. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Reporting directly to the Associate Dean and Senior Director, Career Development Office, the Administrative Coordinator will provide a broad range of support to the Career Development Office (CDO). Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Office Operations & Administrative Tasks (25%) ● Provide administrative support to Senior Director. ● Oversee front desk coverage to ensure CDO is a welcoming space for externals, students and colleagues; meet and greet visitors, students, faculty and staff and field general questions. ● Work collaboratively with the other administrative staff ensure smooth operations, including facilities, housekeeping, deliveries, furniture/supplies, etc. ● Support logistics for large-events, including booking locations, arranging caterers, securing vendors, tracking responses, process payments, etc. Serve as one of the primary technology contacts between the CDO and the web-based recruiting system (presently Handshake) for troubleshooting issues; liaise with ITS to upload student information. ● Design and implement organization systems and processes to improve office functioning and service delivery. ● Arrange travel and hotel accommodation for staff and visitors. ● Schedule/arrange meetings, answer the phone, sort physical mail and inboxes, photocopy and prepare materials for meetings and presentations; provide logistical arrangements for internal and external meetings and videoconferences. Financial Tasks (30%) ● Monitor and administer the departmental budget, track expenditures, process financial transactions, reconcile accounts, and ensure compliance with institutional policies for individual staff, departmental programs and gifts. ● Assist the Senior Director in tracking costs, expenses and budgets of the departments and programs overseen by the Senior Director. ● Identify appropriate vendors for supplies, resources and services; negotiate rates and manage shipments/services rendered. ● Manage office subscriptions and resources. ● Prepare and track business reimbursements; enter purchase requisitions into the institution’s electronic procurement system. Data Management (30%) ● Analyze assessment and benchmarking data and streamline into comprehensive reports for internal and external stakeholders. ● Compile, analyze, and report mid-year and annual data, drawing strategic insights related to student engagement, ofﬁce operations, past performance, and future planning. ● Analyze and report on monthly trends using visual dashboards to communicate operational performance. ● Serve on First Destination and Annual Impact Report teams, support efforts to collect knowledge through outreach, and assist in the data analysis process. ● Educate and train CDO staff around data tracking responsibilities and procedures. ● Create and customize reports, providing data for senior management that will be utilized to increase service and program effectiveness and to inform various constituents about how the CDO is essential to carry out the College’s mission and CDO’s Strategic Plan . Other (15%) ● Serve on CDO Communications team; support Manager of Communications & Digital Media with CDO social media accounts, newsletters, emails, and event marketing. ● The Administrative Coordinator will also assist with special projects and other tasks, as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Bachelor’s degree in business administration or liberal arts is preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience: A minimum of 2 years of administrative experience with increasing responsibility is preferred. At least 2 years of experience at an academic institution is preferred. At least 2 years of data collection and analysis experience preferred. REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE AND CRITICAL SKILLS: This position must possess the knowledge, skills and abilities to be able to successfully perform the essential functions of the position or be able to demonstrate how the essential functions will be performed, with or without reasonable accommodation, using other skills and abilities not listed below. 1. Deploy professional skills in office management, in collaboration with colleagues to best promote the College’s strategic interests. a. Able to exercise good judgment with limited guidance. b. Possess a friendly demeanor that creates a welcoming environment for visitors. c. Possess a professional and flexible demeanor that thrives in an intense, deadline-filled environment, where multi-tasking under pressure is essential. d. Provide good customer service to students, employers, staff, and faculty through a positive attitude, listening to needs, and following up as promised. e. Able to collaborate effectively with all constituents (faculty, staff, colleagues, students, employers) with a good sense of humor, team spirit and positive attitude. f. Knowledgeable of how to supervise and work with students in a liberal arts setting. g. Knowledgeable about CDO resources h. Able to manage events with multiple constituents. i. Able to work well on a variety of projects with a strong team orientation. j. Able to manage and prioritize high levels of email correspondence. 2. Demonstrate effective, accurate and clear communication with excellent verbal, written, interpersonal, reading, and phone skills. Follow all written and verbal instructions, asking questions as needed for clarification of projects/tasks/duties/assignments. 3. Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, etc.) and the ability to quickly learn and effectively use other software platforms and technologies, such as Handshake, Slack, Tableau, Canva, Workday, recruiting systems, databases, and web-based applications. Utilizes assigned technology and equipment to support departmental operations while maintaining confidentiality and data security 4. patience, discretion, good judgment, courtesy and tact while working with people from a wide variety of backgrounds. 5. Prioritize and perform multiple projects/tasks, meet deadlines/timelines, respond to others in a timely manner, and work both independently and as a collaborative member of the College with a high standard of integrity and ethics, in support of the College’s strategic vision and the division’s/department’s annual goals. 6. Use exceptional organizational, administrative and time management skills to complete work with accuracy and a keen attention to detail in a fast-paced environment with constant interruption. 7. Operate the College’s vehicles safely for campus-related work and meet all insurance-related requirements. title: Digital Production Associate
jd_text: ABOUT THE POSITION : The Digital Production Associate (“DPA”) contributes to digital production workflows in an active library environment within the Distinctive Collections & Digital Scholarship Division. Reporting to the Head of Digital Initiatives and Open Publishing, the DPA is responsible for the digitization of textual, photographic, and audiovisual materials associated with The Claremont Colleges Digital Library and other special projects. The DPA contributes to the success of digitization projects through effective collaboration, communication, and by skillful project management and oversight of assigned digital library operations and the special collections scan-on-demand program. Key responsibilities include contributing to the creation, use, migration, and management of digital objects and metadata; contributing to the establishment and improvement of best practices for digitization and publishing workflows, creating documentation, keeping and reporting accurate statistics, training digital production student assistants and temporary project staff; and maintaining effective communication with stakeholders. Priority Deadline: The deadline for first consideration is November 13, 2026. Applications received by this date will receive priority consideration; the position will remain open until filled. Please note that a cover letter and CV/resume are required along with the application. Union: This position is represented by The Claremont Colleges Services Library Staff Federation AFT Local 6735. The employee in this position will be bound by the collective bargaining agreement. COMPENSATION Pay : The pay range for this position is $27.00 - $28.85/hour. Benefits : This position is eligible for our employment benefits package including: 10% retirement contributions after one year (no matching required) Tuition Remission and Professional Development funds Access to fitness facilities Generous time off including 11 paid holidays, up to 22 vacation days and 12 sick days per year, and a paid Winter Closure. Medical, Dental, Vision Work Schedule : The regular hours for this full-time position are 40 hours scheduled from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday for 12 months annually. May be required to work holiday, weekend, and/or evening hours. Regular hours may vary due to the needs of the organization or business unit. This position is not eligible for a hybrid work schedule. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS Digital Production Responsibilities Participates in digital production and publishing workflows for the Claremont Colleges Digital Library (CCDL) and Scholarship@Claremont, with a keen attention to detail and a strong commitment to quality, consistency, accessibility, and long-term digital preservation. Performs quality control of digitized and born-digital content, including imaging, post-processing, audiovisual content, optical character recognition (OCR), metadata, file management, and other digital production activities in accordance with established workflows and standards, including applicable FADGI standards. Participates in the digital collections lifecycle, from digitization and metadata creation through content ingest, publishing, and digital asset management. Supports the Open Publishing Applications Specialist (OPAS) in open publishing production work, including managing the submission of content, creating metadata, designing and documenting workflows, monitoring and ensuring the quality of data, and tracking projects through the publication process. Maintain close and effective communication and reporting on digitization and asset ingest, production issues, and project activities with the Head of Digital Initiatives and Open Publishing. Supports the production and management of video and audio recordings, including AV reformatting and transcription workflows, such as generating, reviewing, correcting and preparing machine-generated transcripts to enhance accessibility and support their use in digital collections and publishing workflows. Responds to email inquiries submitted to the Digital Initiatives LibAnswers queue. Oversee scan-on-demand processes including coordination with related units. Student Assistant Training and Coordination Provides training and guidance to student assistants supporting digitization, scan-on-demand, and audiovisual projects and communicate any issues to the Head of Digital Initiatives and Open Publishing in a timely manner. Assigns and monitors student work and provides training in digitization equipment, imaging, post-processing, quality control, metadata, content ingest, AV reformatting, and file management. Project-related Responsibilities Document procedures and workflows. Track and report on project progress, milestones, and production outputs and communicate issues requiring supervisory attention. Work collaboratively to make recommendations regarding digitization, metadata, quality control, and production workflows. Other Related Duties Perform other related duties as assigned QUALIFICATIONS Education/Training : A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Experience : At least two (2) years of relevant experience in digital production, digitization, digital collections, digital publishing, photography, or a related field, including experience managing digital assets and workflows, creating and maintaining documentation, and applying established standards and procedures to the production of digital content. Other: Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities : Knowledge of digital asset and content management practices,, including metadata, file formats, reformatting and digitization workflows, image capture, post-processing, OCR, quality control, and preservation. Demonstrated ability to manage projects and workflows, prioritize competing tasks, meet deadlines, and ensure the quality and consistency of work General knowledge of audio-visual terminology and equipment. Ability to learn and work effectively with evolving technologies, systems, and digital production tools Ability to analyze and troubleshoot digitization and digital production processes and remediate them. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with colleagues, project partners, and other stakeholders.. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail with a focus on accuracy, quality, accessibility, and long-term digital preservation. Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively in a production-oriented, team environment. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with technology developed or adopted by the archival community for digitizing manuscript material and managing digital content, including familiarity with FADGI guidelines and related digital preservation practices. Experience with or demonstrated interest in applying WCAG standards and best practices for digital content. Experience with capture/conversion and editing software for video and audio files, including ability to troubleshoot audio visual equipment. Experience with digital repository, digital asset management, or publishing platforms such as CONTENTdm and/or bepress. Knowledge of digital preservation principles, standards, and practices. Experience with applications used in digital production such as MS Excel, Adobe Photoshop, etc. Experience using project management tools or methods to coordinate complex, multi-step projects. Physical Requirements: This position primarily performs work in an office environment and requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while working at a computer. The role involves frequent use of a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other standard office equipment, as well as repetitive hand and wrist movements. The position requires the ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, video conference, and electronic communication; read and interpret printed and electronic documents; and exchange accurate information with employees, supervisors, and external partners. Occasional standing, walking, bending, reaching, and lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling materials weighing up to 15 pounds may be required, such as files, office supplies, or computer equipment. title: Operations Manager - Resident Support
jd_text: Tricon is an owner, operator and developer of single-family rental homes in the U.S. and multi-family apartments in Canada. Our commitment to enriching the lives of our employees, residents and local communities underpins Tricon’s culture and business philosophy. We provide high-quality rental housing options for families across the United States and Canada through our technology-enabled operating platform and dedicated on-the-ground operating teams. Our development programs are also delivering thousands of new rental homes and apartments as part of our commitment to help solve the housing supply shortage. Job Description The Operations Manager – Resident Support will be directly responsible for the management and oversight of all resident support within their designated portfolio. This will include all Compliance, Resident Experience & Satisfaction and overall Financial Performance. The Operations Managers – Resident Support will provide direction and guidance to a team of Resident Support Managers. Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following but are not limited to the job specifications contained herein. Additional duties or job functions that can be performed safely may be required as deemed necessary by supervisory personnel. Management Objectives: Ensure all residents are treated with dignity and respect in every interaction Cultivate a culture that is fun, collaborative, and nurturing, where team members feel valued and empowered Offer guidance and support to their team to accomplish Tricon's monthly Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) goals and mid-year reviews. Lead and mentor team members to cultivate their potential as future Tricon leaders, while also enhancing their capacity to deliver exceptional resident support Create a clearly defined roadmap for team members to assist them in meeting company expectations and to achieve their personal goals Understand and achieve their portfolio’s target metrics, goals, and overall portfolio performance in order to effectively guide the team to achieve desired results Hold weekly team meeting to review Resident issues and support team to strategize solutions to resolve any potential escalations Ensure that all team members are properly trained and that they have the appropriate tools to succeed Display exceptional knowledge of Tricon’s policies, processes, and initiatives Alert all appropriate management/parties immediately of any potential habitability/legal/escalated resident concerns/HR issues Communicate promptly and effectively any company updates, financial results, and new objectives with team members Enforce/Manage team compliance with schedules, policies, processes, and procedures to ensure optimal performance and a consistent customer experience Team Objectives: Oversee management of the Acquisition and Disposition Processes Ensure team provides seamless resident move in experience by serving as sole point of contact and resident liaison for approved applicants through 15 days post move in Ensure team educates residents on the appropriate support channels and assure them that your team is available to assist if they encounter any service issues Review all appropriate daily/weekly/monthly reporting for accuracy Work collaboratively with other departments and centralized teams to ensure all team timelines, expectations, standards and goals are met, and to provide support and assist with communication when needed to ensure the team functions cohesively to achieve results and prevent gaps in resident experience Sign all new move in leases in a timely manner Audit SODA/scope documents for accurate resident chargebacks, and ensure that all deposit statements are submitted in a timely manner to remain in compliance with state laws Support all team members to resolve resident escalations as they arise Communication/Character Objectives: Provide excellent customer service to both internal and external customers, going above and beyond the requirements of role to exceed company standards Collaborate cross-functionally with other departments to resolve issues, provide insight and creative solutions, and give feedback on current processes/tools when needed Hold self and team accountable to all budgets, goals, metrics and company initiatives as well as demonstrate Tricon Guiding Principles in all interactions Qualifications: To be successful in this role, you should possess the following qualifications: Ability to analyze multiple data sets and make sound business recommendations accordingly Collaborative, team player Ability to think critically and solve problems Excellent time management skills Adaptable to change and forward thinking Excellent communication skills both written and verbal Ability to work well using mobile office electronic tools and systems Basic accounting and math skills, excellent analytical skills Excellent Customer Service Skills required Knowledge of Yardi preferred Desire for continuous development Minimum Requirements: BA/BS preferred or equivalent experience At least 5 years of property management experience Demonstrated attention to detail Basic financial acumen Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, including: Frequently required to sit; talk; and hear. Occasionally required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and stoop; kneel; or crouch. Occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision and depth perception. At Tricon, we are committed to creating a workplace where every individual is valued for their unique contributions, experiences, voices, and backgrounds.
